318	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
319	
320	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
321	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
322	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
323	no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
324	unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
325	many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
326	second approval by an owner of the same stack, which keeps it to two people (OD8). Confirmed by the owner
327	(OD13): the original author opens the approval PR and the first approver
328	approves it. If the first approver is unavailable, another owner of the stack approves; that makes
329	three people and is recorded as a deviation, counted monthly (OD11). A cross-team PR needs one
330	approval, as GitHub accepts one on-call group member for files of several owner teams (OD10,
331	OD9, 📖 R3.2.7); domain review there is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. A real-data read is not a change and has its own rule, L3-data. Incidents use the same
332	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
333	
334	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
335	|---|---|---|---|---|
336	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
337	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
338	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
339	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue and the rest of the canonical list in layer 5; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, the SCP stack): the L3 owner team only (OD13); IAM-only stacks are deployable, so the L3 owner team plus the on-call group (OD9). L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver for deployable paths (OD9); paths that define the process (CODEOWNERS, agent config, catalogue, workflows) wait for the L3 owner team | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
340	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); incidents only, as the owner accepted it (Options §9 Q2); the on-call approver counts as owner of the service in the request (OD13) | layer 7 |
341	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9; at night, see layer 6 | layer 6 |
342	
343	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
344	the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
345	owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
346	What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned in CODEOWNERS by a designated
347	L3 owner team (deployable L3 paths also by the on-call group, OD9), L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the
348	risk stop. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files, so they are approved by
349	the stack's owners, not the L3 team (OD8); automated checks make up for this: IAM Access Analyzer
350	`check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and the Pulumi policy pack (📖 R4.2.2), both from phase 2 (layer 5). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need the L3 owner team, not
351	the domain team that edits it most.
352	
353	**On Papaya's stack**
354	
355	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
356	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
357	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
358	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
359	  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
360	- **L3 approvals [design]:** CODEOWNERS plus code-owner review only, no path-based required
361	  reviewers rule. That rule (📖 R3.2.4) asks for approvals from specific teams, which the on-call
362	  group would not satisfy at night, and how it combines several teams is not researched (⚠️), so it
363	  would break OD9 or add a third person. GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5), set by a dedicated GitHub App that reacts to review events and is the pinned source [design; hosting, key storage and whether its key counts against S2 are not researched, ⚠️ G19], adds what
364	  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
365	  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3). A workflow
366	  instead of an app is weaker: pinning the source to GitHub Actions likely lets any workflow set a
367	  check of the same name, and the trigger that runs on review events from trusted code is not
368	  researched (⚠️ G19).
369	- **Who approves at night (OD9):** a fixed GitHub team with write permission (owners without it
370	  are silently not assigned, 📖 R3.2.7; the CODEOWNERS validation check covers this), the on-call approvers, is listed as
371	  co-owner on every deployable path in CODEOWNERS (infrastructure and service code), next to the
372	  domain team. Confirmed by the owner (OD13): the group does **not** co-own the paths that
373	  define the process (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md` and agent config, catalogue); those stay
374	  with the L3 owner team only. If a broken workflow blocks a night fix, the pipeline counts as
375	  unavailable and the JIT fallback applies (layer 7). One primary and one backup from that team are on call. Technically any member can approve any
376	  path; by rule the primary approves and the backup only if the primary is unavailable (OD2).
377	  Membership is fixed, not changed per shift [design]. GitHub team membership is set in organization
378	  settings, not by a PR; managing it as code (e.g. with Pulumi's GitHub provider) and the audit
379	  event for a membership change are not researched (⚠️ G16). Meanwhile the layer-7 settings
380	  comparison includes the group's member list. Cost: an approval from any
381	  listed owner satisfies code-owner review (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days a member could approve
382	  another domain's PR, on or off shift. Mitigation [design]: process rule "approve another
383	  domain's PR only if it carries the `incident` label and you are on shift", and a monthly report of
384	  every cross-domain approval by group members on PRs without that label (layer 7). Whether Papaya's team size allows full coverage is unknown
385	  (§1, S7).
386	- **Risk stop [design]:** applies to every deploy, whatever the level. The deploy job previews prod;
387	  on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change, a network or security-group change, or an advisory
388	  policy finding (from phase 2) it stops and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a second PR that adds
389	  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` (`<sha>` = the stopped commit) holding that SHA and the
390	  preview hash; the workflow does not open it, because the setting that lets Actions create and approve PRs stays
391	  off (📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3). CODEOWNERS on `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` names the owners of that stack and the
392	  on-call group (OD8, OD9). The approver is ≠ author and may be the first PR's approver, who now sees
393	  which prod resources and properties change; values stay out of the summary to keep secrets out
394	  of logs, and are reviewed in the code of the stopped PR. Merging it triggers the deploy on the new HEAD, which previews again and continues
395	  only if the hash matches the approved one; if another PR merged in between, the hash differs and
396	  the deploy stops again (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). The approval is bound to git
397	  history, not only to the hash (six conditions, 7-day expiry; examples E7, finding 2) [design].
398	  Known gap (OD18): an early approval can match a later change outside the stack (G19 closes it: the app checks that the stopped run's summary carries the same hash).
399	  The stop catches risky diffs nobody looked at, not approved malicious code (OD15); OD22 limits what such code can reach (layer 5). Cost: while a stack is
400	  stopped, later merges to that stack stop too until a matching approval lands; in an incident, a
401	  risky change already waiting on `main` blocks the fix for the same stack until it is approved or
402	  reverted. A
403	  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
404	  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
405	  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
406	- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
407	  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
408	  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
409	  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4); squash-only merges, so each PR is one commit on
410	  `main` (OD16); and the job deploys only the current tip of `main`, because a writer can re-run an
411	  old run for 30 days and roll prod back without approval (OD17; 📖 GitHub docs, linked in examples finding 4).
412	- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
413	  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
414	  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
415	  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
416	  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
417	- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
418	  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
419	  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
420	  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
421	- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
422	  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
423	- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
424	  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1). The risk
425	  stop is described for Pulumi and Serverless only; for k0s manifests (RBAC changes are the IAM
426	  equivalent) a `kubectl diff`-based stop is a candidate, not researched (⚠️ G1). Firebase deploys
427	  have no preview step in this design (⚠️ G2).
428	- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
429	  slow unrelated tests skipped [design]. A required check skipped by a path filter may stay
430	  pending and block the merge (open, Options §8); this directly affects S7.
431	
432	**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)
433	
434	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
435	unavailable).
436	
437	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
438	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
439	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
440	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
441	3. R, a co-owner of `serverless.yml` through the on-call group (OD9), reviews the diff. If R
442	   catches a missing queue change, R does not fix it (OD7): E pushes the fix, the stale approval is
443	   dismissed, and R approves again, one more review round (Options §6). E merges.
444	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
445	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.
446	
447	**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks), the deploy run log and risk-stop summary (exported, retention ⚠️ G7), the `deploy-approvals/` PR, and CloudTrail events linked by commit SHA and run ID; walk-through: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#evidence-for-one-prod-change-s8).
448	
449	**Cost / value.** One approver for every prod change, from the owners of the path; two approvals,

449	**Cost / value.** One approver for every prod change, from the owners of the path; two approvals,
450	usually by the same approver, when the risk stop fires (OD13; OD11). Cross-team PRs: one approval (OD10). None in non-prod.
451	Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

490	## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening
491	
492	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
493	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
494	checks as human code (S10).
495	
496	**On Papaya's stack**
497	
498	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
499	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
500	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
501	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
502	  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
503	  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
504	  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
505	  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
506	    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
507	    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
508	    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
509	    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
510	  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
511	    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
512	    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). Self-hosted runners "can be persistently
513	    compromised by untrusted code" from anyone who can open a PR, and runner groups limit only which
514	    repositories use them (📖 R3.5.2); in a monorepo any workflow can likely target the runner's label (⚠️ G15).
515	    How to restrict a runner to one workflow is not researched (⚠️ G15); just-in-time runners exist
516	    (📖 R3.5.2, not read in detail). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
517	    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
518	  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
519	  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register;
520	  - a separate environment `production-k0s` (required since OD24, was optional), limited to
521	    `main` and referenced only by the k0s/Firebase deploy workflow, so AWS deploy jobs cannot read
522	    these secrets [design];
523	  - for k0s, the credential is the namespaced, time-limited ServiceAccount token of layer 1
524	    (OD24), rotated before it expires, and the cluster writes a Kubernetes API audit log: k0s has
525	    none by default and enables it only through `spec.api.extraArgs`, "outside k0s support"
526	    (📖 R9.3.1, R9.3.2). Secrets and token requests are logged at `Metadata` level so their
527	    contents stay out of the log (📖 R9.3.3; examples E11). A leaked token is then limited to
528	    deploys in its namespaces and leaves a trace; shipping that log to the log archive is part
529	    of G1.
530	
531	  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
532	  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
533	  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
534	  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
535	  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
536	- **What runs in the deploy job (OD22, phase 1).** Approved code runs with a prod deploy role:
537	  the Pulumi program during preview and apply, Serverless plugins, and any install script.
538	  The risk stop sees resources, not SDK calls the program makes while it runs, so it cannot
539	  catch this (OD15). Three controls limit the damage instead [design]:
540	  - **one environment per kind of stack:** the IAM stack deploys from `production-iam`, every
541	    other stack from `production`; each has its own OIDC subject and roles, so a domain stack's
542	    job cannot obtain the IAM stack's role (layer 1; examples E3, E4);
543	  - **domain roles are bounded:** they create or change only `svc-*` roles carrying the fixed
544	    permissions boundary (layer 1);
545	  - **no install scripts:** `npm_config_ignore_scripts` is set for the whole deploy and preview
546	    job ("npm does not run scripts specified in package.json files", 📖 R9.1.13; whether this
547	    covers every dependency is ⚠️ until tested on the runner). Packages that need their script
548	    are listed in `tools/ci/allowed-install-scripts.txt`, an L3 path, and rebuilt one by one
549	    (`npm rebuild <pkg>`, 📖 R9.1.13). npm v11 also has an `allowScripts` policy (📖 R9.1.13),
550	    an alternative once the CI npm version is known.
551	
552	  What stays: malicious code inside one stack can still do what that stack's role allows. The
553	  separate preview role of OD15 stays on the phase-2 roadmap (item 2.9), because `pulumi up`
554	  runs the same program again with the apply role.
555	- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
556	  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
557	- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
558	  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA" (availability on Team ⚠️); the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so

603	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
604	
605	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
606	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
607	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
608	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
609	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
610	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
611	
612	**On Papaya's stack**
613	
614	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
615	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role from
616	    phase 1 (existing broad read roles are removed) and the SCP from phase 2
617	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
618	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
619	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
620	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
621	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
622	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
623	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
624	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. At night the data owner is not on call: the
625	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day. This
626	  applies to non-PHI and PHI alike; for PHI the reader is still a human without an agent. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
627	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
628	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
629	    redacted summary. This
630	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
631	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
632	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
633	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
634	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
635	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
636	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
637	  1.11.4 L6).
638	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default (sandboxed Bash runs without a prompt, layer 2); the auto-mode
639	  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions and 5.7 % of 1,000 synthetic exfiltration
640	  attempts (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path
641	  (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no WebFetch, likely no edit tools (layer 2), and runs outside
642	  the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
643	  commands (layer 2), including the SSO token cache; "no standing write, no PHI read" limits what
644	  the token opens, except during a JIT or data-read window (layer 2 mitigations). Shared knowledge
645	  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is exempt from the protected-path rules unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
646	- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
647	  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
648	  (GĐ-3, unconfirmed).
649	- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
650	  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14: until cleaned, non-prod follows the GĐ-9 data-read rule). Cost: until scanned, that store is
651	  not part of the free loop.
652	- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
653	  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
654	- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
655	  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
656	  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).
657	
658	**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data, real-data requests with the data-read role's CloudTrail events, and non-prod scan results; full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).

659	
660	**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
661	Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2;
662	actions ⚠️ G13) and by process
663	elsewhere, and a record per exception (S9).

667	## Layer 7 — Observability, audit, incident response and break-glass
668	
669	**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
670	named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
671	is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.
672	
673	**On Papaya's stack**
674	
675	- **Audit stores:**
676	  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
677	    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
678	    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (cost 📖 R2.6.3; selection
679	    ⚠️ R2.9 #5), which makes the archive
680	    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
681	  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
682	  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
683	    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
684	    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
685	    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
686	    with an expected copy (G8);
687	  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
688	    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
689	  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2);
690	  - Kubernetes API audit log of prod k0s (OD24, layer 5); destination open (G1).
691	- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
692	  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
693	  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
694	  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
695	- **Drift [design]:** its own role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
696	  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
697	  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
698	  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
699	  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
700	  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
701	  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
702	  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
703	  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
704	  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
705	- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7), as
706	  decided in framing round 1, and, because of OD7, a minimal incident-responder schedule; the
707	  latter extends that decision. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
708	  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
709	  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
710	  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5); in phase 1 the responder calls the approver by phone from the published schedule.
711	- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:
712	
713	  | Step | Rule |
714	  |---|---|
715	  | When | Only during an incident (Options §9 Q2), when the PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. Outside incidents, an operation not in IaC waits for IaC or a runbook. |
716	  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
717	  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (Options §4b; OD7; backup rule OD2). |
718	  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). Applying it is a management-account change held by the L3 owner team only, and no night-time path for it is designed yet (⚠️ G20): until one exists, a misused grant may run to the end of its window. Candidate: a pre-approved revocation runbook for one named L3 owner reachable by phone, or an org-wide `aws:TokenIssueTime` Deny as kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3). |
719	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
720	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
721	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
722	
723	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
724	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
725	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
726	
727	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
728	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
729	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
730	  this draft). On a breach,
731	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
732	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
733	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
734	  (D2, ⚠️).
735	
736	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail, the exported GitHub audit log, change records and monthly reconciliation (S3, S8), JIT records, drift tickets and incident approval waits (S7); full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).
737	
738	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
739	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
740	incidents, plus detection.

744	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
745	
746	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
747	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
748	attacks.
749	
750	**On Papaya's stack**
751	
752	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
753	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
754	  Applicability); engineering leads (decide CODEOWNERS content; changes to it are approved by the L3 owner team); engineering management (on-call schedule).
755	- **Policy as code:** catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are files under
756	  CODEOWNERS. Settings that live outside files are kept as an expected copy in git and compared with
757	  the live state: GitHub settings (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8) and Claude managed settings, which are edited in
758	  the admin console (📖 R1.1.5; comparison method in layer 2). Few GitHub admins and Claude org
759	  Owners, reviewed quarterly.
760	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
761	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
762	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed): [`03-rollout-plan.md`](03-rollout-plan.md), moved
763	  there with its items unchanged except syncs with the examples' findings (trail deny, allowlist,
764	  phase-2 version floor), and expanded with owners and checks [design]. Order (framing Q8): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials, (2) narrow standing prod
765	  access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2). Phase 1 (0–30 days)
766	  makes the PR the default prod write path, with six hard prerequisites before standing prod write is
767	  removed; phase 2 (30–60) adds SCPs, the rest of the managed baseline and automated
768	  reconciliation; phase 3 (60–90) tests and reviews. The phase-1 load on 1–2 DevSecOps people is the
769	  main rollout risk [design; effort not estimated ⚠️].
770	
771	- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
772	- **Standards mapping:** ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (IDs recalled, ⚠️ R5.1), HIPAA Security Rule
773	  (📖 R5.2) and Vietnam law (📖 R5.4) are mapped per control area in the
774	  [compliance register](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference), with every caveat. "A named human approves"
775	  is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
776	- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.
777	
778	**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files, monthly metrics, 90-day review minutes, the exception register and planted-injection reports; standards: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference).
779	
780	**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and the owners of deploy workflows. Compliance gets a managed system
781	with owners and review dates.

490	## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening
491	
492	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
493	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
494	checks as human code (S10).
495	
496	**On Papaya's stack**
497	
498	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
499	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
500	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
501	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
502	  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
503	  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
504	  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
505	  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
506	    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
507	    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
508	    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
509	    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
510	  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
511	    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
512	    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). Self-hosted runners "can be persistently
513	    compromised by untrusted code" from anyone who can open a PR, and runner groups limit only which
514	    repositories use them (📖 R3.5.2); in a monorepo any workflow can likely target the runner's label (⚠️ G15).
515	    How to restrict a runner to one workflow is not researched (⚠️ G15); just-in-time runners exist
516	    (📖 R3.5.2, not read in detail). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
517	    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
518	  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
519	  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register;
520	  - a separate environment `production-k0s` (required since OD24, was optional), limited to
521	    `main` and referenced only by the k0s/Firebase deploy workflow, so AWS deploy jobs cannot read
522	    these secrets [design];
523	  - for k0s, the credential is the namespaced, time-limited ServiceAccount token of layer 1
524	    (OD24), rotated before it expires, and the cluster writes a Kubernetes API audit log: k0s has
525	    none by default and enables it only through `spec.api.extraArgs`, "outside k0s support"
526	    (📖 R9.3.1, R9.3.2). Secrets and token requests are logged at `Metadata` level so their
527	    contents stay out of the log (📖 R9.3.3; examples E11). A leaked token is then limited to
528	    deploys in its namespaces and leaves a trace; shipping that log to the log archive is part
529	    of G1.
530	
531	  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
532	  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
533	  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
534	  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
535	  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
536	- **What runs in the deploy job (OD22, phase 1).** Approved code runs with a prod deploy role:
537	  the Pulumi program during preview and apply, Serverless plugins, and any install script.
538	  The risk stop sees resources, not SDK calls the program makes while it runs, so it cannot
539	  catch this (OD15). Three controls limit the damage instead [design]:
540	  - **one environment per kind of stack:** the IAM stack deploys from `production-iam`, every
541	    other stack from `production`; each has its own OIDC subject and roles, so a domain stack's
542	    job cannot obtain the IAM stack's role (layer 1; examples E3, E4);
543	  - **domain roles are bounded:** they create or change only `svc-*` roles carrying the fixed
544	    permissions boundary (layer 1);
545	  - **no install scripts:** `npm_config_ignore_scripts` is set for the whole deploy and preview
546	    job ("npm does not run scripts specified in package.json files", 📖 R9.1.13; whether this
547	    covers every dependency is ⚠️ until tested on the runner). Packages that need their script
548	    are listed in `tools/ci/allowed-install-scripts.txt`, an L3 path, and rebuilt one by one
549	    (`npm rebuild <pkg>`, 📖 R9.1.13). npm v11 also has an `allowScripts` policy (📖 R9.1.13),
550	    an alternative once the CI npm version is known.
551	
552	  What stays: malicious code inside one stack can still do what that stack's role allows. The
553	  separate preview role of OD15 stays on the phase-2 roadmap (item 2.9), because `pulumi up`
554	  runs the same program again with the apply role.
555	- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
556	  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
557	- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
558	  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA" (availability on Team ⚠️); the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
559	  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5; conclusion [design]).
560	- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
561	  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, `.devcontainer/` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5, R6.3.11), plus
562	  `.npmrc` (registry redirection) [design], the policy packs, the SCP code, the
563	  catalogue file and the risk-stop classifier `tools/risk-stop/` (OD14: the deploy runs it from the
564	  merged commit, so a domain-approved PR could otherwise switch it off), the install-script allowlist `tools/ci/` (OD22), the Identity Center stack (OD23), and the k0s RBAC and API-server configuration (OD24). This is the canonical L3 path list that layer 3 refers to. Not on it:
565	  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`, owned by the stack's owners and the on-call group (OD8, OD9). The private plugin
566	  marketplace is a separate repo and needs its own ruleset and CODEOWNERS [design]. CI validates the file, because
567	  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7). A fail-safe default line (`*` → L3 owner team and
568	  on-call group) keeps new stacks and root files from being unowned, since an unowned file accepts
569	  an approval from any writer (examples finding 7) [design].
570	- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
571	  📖 R3.5.4).
572	- **Agent review:** an independent agent (not the one that made the change) may post an automated
573	  review as an extra check; it never counts as an approval (GĐ-11). It runs on every PR that
574	  touches `infra/**`, `policy-packs/**` or a `serverless.yml` (OD22), so the human approver of
575	  code that will run with a deploy role always has a second reading of it [design].
576	- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
577	  requests (📖 R1.7.8), whose own credentials are listed in the S2 inventory (⚠️ G19); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);
578	  `--restricted` and explicit `--tools` (D3; passing it through `claude_args` unverified, ⚠️ research
579	  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
580	  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
581	  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),
582	  so with `Bash` in `--tools` the runner file is advisory (⚠️ R3.5.1, R3.6 #4).
583	- **App-opened PRs:** a required check set by a dedicated GitHub App, pinned as its source (layer 3), confirms at least one approval by a
584	  human who did not trigger the run; counting approvals is not enough, since the app's own approval
585	  might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3; 📖 R3.2.5).
586	- **Required checks (S10):** from phase 1, secret scanning, dependency check, SAST (products: G4);
587	  from phase 2, IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and Pulumi policy packs
588	  (📖 R4.2.2). For Serverless stacks, Access Analyzer would check the IAM policies in the
589	  CloudFormation template that `serverless package` produces, against the deployed ones (⚠️ not
590	  researched); policy packs do not apply to them. Until phase 2, the only compensation for OD8 is
591	  the risk stop, which fires on every IAM change in the prod preview. A mandatory policy is only
592	  advisory during a preview while a value is still unknown (✅ `@pulumi/policy` 1.21.0 source,

594	  (E10) also lists the routes it does not cover.
595	
596	**Audit evidence.** Workflows and lockfile in git, the secrets inventory and exception register (S2), audit-log events for secrets and Actions settings, and check results per PR; full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).
597	
598	**Cost / value.** One-time migration to OIDC and pinned actions; slower action updates. Compliance

603	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
604	
605	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
606	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
607	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
608	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
609	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
610	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
611	
612	**On Papaya's stack**
613	
614	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
615	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role from
616	    phase 1 (existing broad read roles are removed) and the SCP from phase 2
617	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
618	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
619	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
620	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
621	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
622	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
623	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
624	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. At night the data owner is not on call: the
625	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day. This
626	  applies to non-PHI and PHI alike; for PHI the reader is still a human without an agent. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
627	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
628	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
629	    redacted summary. This
630	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
631	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
632	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
633	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
634	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
635	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
636	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
637	  1.11.4 L6).
638	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default (sandboxed Bash runs without a prompt, layer 2); the auto-mode
639	  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions and 5.7 % of 1,000 synthetic exfiltration
640	  attempts (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path
641	  (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no WebFetch, likely no edit tools (layer 2), and runs outside
642	  the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
643	  commands (layer 2), including the SSO token cache; "no standing write, no PHI read" limits what
644	  the token opens, except during a JIT or data-read window (layer 2 mitigations). Shared knowledge
645	  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is exempt from the protected-path rules unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
646	- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
647	  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
648	  (GĐ-3, unconfirmed).
649	- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
650	  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14: until cleaned, non-prod follows the GĐ-9 data-read rule). Cost: until scanned, that store is
651	  not part of the free loop.
652	- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
653	  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
654	- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
655	  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
656	  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).
657	
658	**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data, real-data requests with the data-read role's CloudTrail events, and non-prod scan results; full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).

659	
660	**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
661	Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2;
662	actions ⚠️ G13) and by process
663	elsewhere, and a record per exception (S9).

667	## Layer 7 — Observability, audit, incident response and break-glass
668	
669	**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
670	named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
671	is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.
672	
673	**On Papaya's stack**
674	
675	- **Audit stores:**
676	  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
677	    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
678	    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (cost 📖 R2.6.3; selection
679	    ⚠️ R2.9 #5), which makes the archive
680	    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
681	  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
682	  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
683	    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
684	    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
685	    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
686	    with an expected copy (G8);
687	  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
688	    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
689	  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2);
690	  - Kubernetes API audit log of prod k0s (OD24, layer 5); destination open (G1).
691	- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
692	  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
693	  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
694	  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
695	- **Drift [design]:** its own role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
696	  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
697	  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
698	  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
699	  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
700	  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
701	  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
702	  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
703	  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
704	  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
705	- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7), as
706	  decided in framing round 1, and, because of OD7, a minimal incident-responder schedule; the
707	  latter extends that decision. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
708	  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
709	  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
710	  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5); in phase 1 the responder calls the approver by phone from the published schedule.
711	- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:
712	
713	  | Step | Rule |
714	  |---|---|
715	  | When | Only during an incident (Options §9 Q2), when the PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. Outside incidents, an operation not in IaC waits for IaC or a runbook. |
716	  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
717	  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (Options §4b; OD7; backup rule OD2). |
718	  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). Applying it is a management-account change held by the L3 owner team only, and no night-time path for it is designed yet (⚠️ G20): until one exists, a misused grant may run to the end of its window. Candidate: a pre-approved revocation runbook for one named L3 owner reachable by phone, or an org-wide `aws:TokenIssueTime` Deny as kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3). |
719	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
720	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
721	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
722	
723	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
724	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
725	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
726	
727	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
728	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
729	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
730	  this draft). On a breach,
731	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
732	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
733	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
734	  (D2, ⚠️).
735	
736	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail, the exported GitHub audit log, change records and monthly reconciliation (S3, S8), JIT records, drift tickets and incident approval waits (S7); full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).
737	
738	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
739	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
740	incidents, plus detection.
741	
742	---
743	
744	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
745	
746	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
747	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
748	attacks.
749	
750	**On Papaya's stack**
751	
752	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
753	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
754	  Applicability); engineering leads (decide CODEOWNERS content; changes to it are approved by the L3 owner team); engineering management (on-call schedule).
755	- **Policy as code:** catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are files under
756	  CODEOWNERS. Settings that live outside files are kept as an expected copy in git and compared with
757	  the live state: GitHub settings (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8) and Claude managed settings, which are edited in
758	  the admin console (📖 R1.1.5; comparison method in layer 2). Few GitHub admins and Claude org
759	  Owners, reviewed quarterly.
760	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
761	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
762	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed): [`03-rollout-plan.md`](03-rollout-plan.md), moved
763	  there with its items unchanged except syncs with the examples' findings (trail deny, allowlist,
764	  phase-2 version floor), and expanded with owners and checks [design]. Order (framing Q8): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials, (2) narrow standing prod
765	  access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2). Phase 1 (0–30 days)
766	  makes the PR the default prod write path, with six hard prerequisites before standing prod write is
767	  removed; phase 2 (30–60) adds SCPs, the rest of the managed baseline and automated
768	  reconciliation; phase 3 (60–90) tests and reviews. The phase-1 load on 1–2 DevSecOps people is the
769	  main rollout risk [design; effort not estimated ⚠️].
770	
771	- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
772	- **Standards mapping:** ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (IDs recalled, ⚠️ R5.1), HIPAA Security Rule
773	  (📖 R5.2) and Vietnam law (📖 R5.4) are mapped per control area in the
774	  [compliance register](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference), with every caveat. "A named human approves"
775	  is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
776	- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.
777	
778	**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files, monthly metrics, 90-day review minutes, the exception register and planted-injection reports; standards: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference).
779	
780	**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and the owners of deploy workflows. Compliance gets a managed system
781	with owners and review dates.
782	
783	---
784	
785	## Gaps (not covered, or only as an open item, in `work/02-research.md`)
786	
787	| # | Gap | Layers |
788	|---|---|---|
789	| G1 | k0s: human authentication and RBAC (GĐ-4); placing the audit policy on controllers and shipping the audit log; the target OIDC trust on Papaya's k0s version (OD24 gives interim controls); break-glass when Actions is down | 1, 3, 6, 7 |
790	| G2 | Firebase Hosting deploy from CI without a stored token; break-glass when Actions is down | 1, 5, 7 |
791	| G3 | Human and agent access to GCP (roles, data access) | 1, 6 |
792	| G4 | Secret scanning, dependency check, SAST, non-prod data scanning on the Team plan | 5, 6 |
793	| G5 | Paging and alert routing; approving a PR from a phone | 7 |
794	| G6 | SSM Automation `aws:approve` (read in `work/03-options.md` §2, not in 02-research) | 7 |
795	| G7 | GitHub Actions log and artifact retention, and export | 3, 7 |
796	| G8 | Rulesets and environment settings through the API | 7, 8 |
797	| G9 | How Linear and Slack MCP servers authenticate | 4, 6 |
798	| G10 | OIDC subject customisation (`job_workflow_ref`) on GitHub Team | 1 |
799	| G11 | Closing provider/login bypasses on laptops without MDM | 2 |
800	| G12 | `pulumi up` flag reference for the prod allowlist | 3 |
801	| G13 | IAM actions for every data-plane read (S3, SQS, Step Functions, Secrets Manager, RDS, ECS Exec, Lambda invoke) | 1, 6 |
802	| G14 | Which state writes a Pulumi refresh preview needs on a DIY S3 backend | 3, 7 |
803	| G15 | Restricting a self-hosted runner to one workflow in a monorepo; just-in-time runners | 5 |
804	| G16 | Managing GitHub team membership as code; audit event for a membership change | 3, 7 |
805	| G17 | Who forms the L3 owner team and how many people (GĐ-1: never a single reviewer) | 3, 8 |
806	| G18 | Reading the live values of server-managed settings (API or local cache) to compare with git | 2, 8 |
807	| G19 | Required-check app and CI-agent app: review-event triggers, source pinning against same-name checks, hosting, private-key storage and whether those keys count against S2; the app's check that a risk-stop approval matches the stopped run's hash (OD18) | 3, 5 |
808	| G20 | Emergency revocation at night: who can apply the revocation Deny SCP (management account) within minutes; `aws:TokenIssueTime` kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3) | 1, 7 |
809	
810	Open checks from `work/03-options.md` §8 remain open.
811	
812	## Owner decisions (2026-11-09)
813	
814	The owner answered the open questions of draft v3. English rendering; the original Vietnamese
815	answers are recorded in `work/session-log.md`.
816	
817	| # | Question | Decision |
818	|---|---|---|
819	| OD1 | Exception to S2 = 0 for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials? | Yes, provided each credential has a single source of truth. (The first reason given, continuous scale-in/scale-out, concerns runtime credentials; OD6 narrowed the scope.) |
820	| OD2 | L3: must one approver be from the platform team? | Not necessarily; one approval procedure is agreed for all engineers, and the on-call engineer is enough. Clarified in follow-ups: every change involves two people, one who makes it and one who approves; the on-call backup only replaces an unavailable primary. Asked whether L3 should need more approvers than L2, the owner chose "L3 = 1 approver at all times"; in the agent's framing of that option, the approver must own the path. |
821	| OD3 | `CLAUDE.md` changes: L2 or L3? | L3, because the workflow must be consistent across the whole team. |
822	| OD4 | Move the rest of the managed baseline and the SSM check to phase 2? | Yes. |
823	| OD5 | "An agent does not approve PRs" only a process rule? | It is a rule: the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent. |
824	| OD6 | Scope of OD1: CI deploy credentials only, or also runtime scaling credentials? | CI deploy credentials (k0s kubeconfig/token, Firebase token in GitHub secrets) only, until it is checked whether k0s and Firebase can use OIDC. |
825	| OD7 | (a) If the on-call engineer writes an L3 fix, who approves? (b) Keep the read-only allowlist in phase 1? | (a) "While on call, never change the process"; clarified: on-call engineers only approve, and fixes are written by another engineer (the incident responder), so the approver is never the author. (b) Yes, as proposed. |
826	| OD8 | IAM/network/stateful changes inside a domain file: who approves the risk stop? | The stack's owners (may be the first approver); always two people. The L3 owner team keeps only the real L3 paths; Access Analyzer and policy packs compensate. |
827	| OD9 | How can one on-call primary approve any path at night? | The on-call approver group co-owns every deployable path; one primary + one backup. Normal-day domain review is a process rule with a monthly check. |
828	| OD10 | A PR touching files of several domain teams: split, or one approval? | One approval is enough (two-person rule kept); domain review on such PRs is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. |
829	| OD11 | Risk stop when the first approver is unavailable: may another owner of the stack approve? | Yes; it makes three people and is recorded as a deviation. |
830	| OD12 | `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`: `true` or `false`? | Keep `true` (fewer prompts, relies on the sandbox, which arrives in phase 2). |
831	| OD13 | Confirm three agent readings: (1) OD8, who opens and approves the risk-stop approval PR; (2) OD9, scope of the on-call group; (3) L3-JIT, does the on-call approver count as service owner? | Confirmed: (1) the original author opens it and the first approver approves it; (2) the on-call group does not co-own process-defining paths or the SCP stack, which only the L3 owner team approves; (3) yes. |
832	| OD14 | Add the risk-stop classifier (`tools/risk-stop/`) to the canonical L3 path list? (found while writing `examples/`) | Yes: it is a control, so only the L3 owner team may change it. |
833	| OD15 | Scope of the risk stop: risky diffs nobody looked at, or also malicious approved code? | Keep the current scope and state its limits; a separate prod preview role and a job split go to the phase-2 roadmap. |
834	| OD16 | Squash-only merges to `main` (needed so a PR cannot carry its own risk-stop approval)? | Yes; the cost is that PR-internal commit history is not kept on `main`. |
835	| OD17 | Deploy only the current tip of `main`, so re-running an old run cannot roll prod back? | Yes; added to the layer-3 "merge approval = deploy approval" conditions. |
836	| OD18 | An approval merged before a deploy stops, matched by a later change outside the stack's directory, is still accepted | Accepted as a stated limit; the approval-gate app (G19) is to close it by checking the stopped run's hash. |
837	| OD19 | Protect the names of SCP-exempt roles (`app-claims-*`, `cfn-deployment-*`, `github-prod-deploy-*`) so that only the IAM stack's deploy role can create or change them? (found while writing `examples/`) | Yes. Confirmed reading: "only the IAM stack" holds once OD20 gives the IAM stack its own role and OIDC subject; until then the protection is "only an approved prod Pulumi deploy". OD22 gives the IAM stack that role and subject in phase 1. |
838	| OD20 | Code in the deploy job (install scripts, Pulumi program, Serverless plugins) can request the job's OIDC token for either prod deploy role: fix now or roadmap? | Roadmap phase 2, together with OD15: a build job without `id-token`, and per-role environments (different OIDC subjects) or `job_workflow_ref`. Until then it is a stated limit. **Superseded in timing by OD22:** per-environment roles move to phase 1. |
839	| OD21 | Phase 1 lets built-in read-only commands (`cat`, `head` …) read `~/.aws` without a prompt, and allow rules skip the auto-mode classifier: add keys to the phase-1 subset? | Yes: add a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule and `autoMode.classifyAllShell: true` (examples finding 19). |
840	
841	**Fixes after the independent review** (`work/07-review.md`; proposals and the owner's choices in
842	`work/08-fix-proposals.md`, documentation checks in `work/09-fix-research.md`). The owner accepted
843	every proposal on 2026-11-09:
844	
845	| # | Review finding | Decision |
846	|---|---|---|
847	| OD22 | Approved code runs with a prod deploy role, which can change SCP-exempt roles (review A-1) | Moves OD20 into phase 1: the IAM stack gets its own environment `production-iam` and role; domain deploy roles change only `svc-*` roles under a fixed permissions boundary; no install scripts in deploy and preview jobs except a reviewed allowlist (L3 path); agent review on every PR touching infrastructure code. The separate preview role (OD15) stays in phase 2. |
848	| OD23 | Identity Center administrators and `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` can grant prod write outside the design (review C-4) | Identity Center permission sets and assignments as code (L3 owner team only) with alerts on other changes; an SCP denies `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` in the prod OU; member-account root credentials removed; a named management-account group. |

1	# Engineer guide: working with Claude Code at Papaya
     2	
     3	> Status: a summary of the approved framework; it adds no rule · Updated: 2026-11-09 · Builds on
     4	> [`01-framework.md`](01-framework.md)
     5	
     6	This page answers one question: **what changes in my working day?** Each section says what you do,
     7	who approves, and how long it takes. The rules and their sources are in the framework layer linked
     8	from each section; if this page and the framework differ, the framework wins. Times are targets from
     9	the success criteria (S-n) or estimates marked ⚠️.
    10	
    11	## The short version
    12	
    13	- **Non-prod is yours.** Build, deploy and debug in non-prod with the agent, with no new approval (S4),
    14	  once a store has been scanned for real data (until then it follows the real-data rule, section 5).
    15	- **Prod reads are metrics and metadata.** No standing prod write for anyone, you included.
    16	- **Every prod change is a pull request.** One code owner who is not you approves; CI applies it.
    17	- **In an incident the path is the same, with faster people:** an on-call approver, 24/7.
    18	- **Real customer data, new tools and break-glass need a request.** Each has a named approver and a time limit.
    19	
    20	## 1. Daily development (non-prod)
    21	
    22	- **What you do:** use Claude Code as you do today, with non-prod roles. Manual permission mode is the
    23	  default; you may switch to auto mode (D1). Commands that run inside the sandbox run without a prompt
    24	  (phase 2, OD12).
    25	- **Approval:** none (risk level L1).
    26	- **What is different:** the organisation's managed settings apply to everyone; bypass mode is
    27	  removed; plugins and MCP servers come from the catalogue only (section 6). From phase 2 the sandbox
    28	  hides credentials and blocks Unix sockets, so `git push`, `gh`, Docker and private-registry `npm ci` fail inside it: run
    29	  them yourself at the `!` prompt. Using `--restricted` is recommended (D3).
    30	- **From phase 2 you will also notice** (layer 2, examples E8): each `aws`, `pulumi` or `serverless`
    31	  call asks you first, in auto mode too; each WebFetch asks; your own and the project's permission
    32	  rules are ignored, so prompts may rise; sign-in is locked to Papaya's organisation (API-key sessions
    33	  are refused) and the minimum Claude Code version rises; on macOS, servers on localhost fail inside
    34	  the sandbox; native Windows is not supported (use WSL2).
    35	- **Layer:** [2](01-framework.md#layer-2--agent-runtime-controls).
    36	
    37	## 2. Reading prod
    38	
    39	- **What you do:** with `ProdReadMetadata` (1-hour session) you and your agent read metrics, metadata
    40	  and logs that are redacted at source. Lambda configuration is readable per service once its secrets
    41	  are resolved at runtime; until then, read timeout and memory from the IaC code.
    42	- **Approval:** none (L0).
    43	- **Cost to know:** in the first months, raw logs of services not yet redacted are not readable
    44	  without a data-read request (section 5). This is the largest cost of the transition.
    45	- **Remember:** the agent uses **your** AWS SSO session, so it can do whatever you can (layer 1). Keep
    46	  the portal session short.
    47	- **Layer:** [1](01-framework.md#layer-1--identity-and-access).
    48	
    49	## 3. Shipping a prod change
    50	
    51	1. Write the change as code (Pulumi, `serverless.yml`, Kubernetes manifests) and preview it on non-prod.
    52	2. Push the branch and open a pull request. The PR runs secret scanning, dependency checks and SAST
    53	   (S10), and previews non-prod only.
    54	3. One code owner of the changed files approves. You cannot approve your own PR, and the approver may
    55	   not be the last person who pushed. An agent never approves a PR (OD5).
    56	   - Domain code and stacks: your domain team. Members of the on-call group are co-owners, but by
    57	     rule they approve another domain's PR only if it is labelled `incident` and they are on shift;
    58	     other cases appear in a monthly report (OD9).
    59	   - Process files (`.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, the catalogue, the SCP stack,
    60	     `tools/risk-stop/`): the L3 owner team only.
    61	4. Merge (squash only). The deploy job previews prod and applies the change.
    62	5. **If the deploy stops at the risk stop** (stateful replace or delete, IAM, network, a policy
    63	   finding): open a second PR that adds only `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<stopped commit>.yaml` with the
    64	   hash from the job summary. By default the first approver approves it; if they are unavailable,
    65	   another owner of the stack does, which is recorded as a deviation (OD13, OD11). Merging it deploys
    66	   if the new prod preview has the same hash. While the stack is stopped, later merges to it stop too.
    67	
    68	- **Time:** same working day from PR to prod; approval wait ≤ 1 hour in working hours (S4 targets).
    69	- **What CI does differently (OD22):** npm install scripts do not run in preview and deploy jobs;
    70	  if a package needs its script, ask the L3 owner team to add it to `tools/ci/allowed-install-scripts.txt`.
    71	  A stack may create IAM roles for its own services only as `svc-*` roles with the standard
    72	  permissions boundary; roles that read claim data (`app-claims-*`) are created in the IAM stack
    73	  and referenced by ARN. PRs that touch infrastructure code also get an automated agent review,
    74	  which is advice, not an approval.
    75	- **Layer:** [3](01-framework.md#layer-3--change-workflow-by-risk-level); diagram
    76	  [`01-change-workflow`](../diagrams/01-change-workflow.svg).
    77	
    78	## 4. An incident at 2 a.m.
    79	
    80	You are the **incident responder**. The **on-call approver** only approves; they never write the fix (OD7).
    81	
    82	1. Start an incident-analysis session with read-only roles, in an empty scratch directory outside
    83	   the repository: `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"` (no WebFetch; Bash can still reach
    84	   the network). Read metrics and redacted logs.
    85	2. Make the fix in a normal session, preview on non-prod, open a PR labelled `incident`.
    86	3. Call the on-call approver (phone in phase 1; routed alerts from phase 2). They review and approve.
    87	   If they find a problem, you push the fix and they approve again.
    88	4. Merge; the deploy job applies the change.
    89	
    90	- **Time:** target ≤ 15 min waiting for approval (S7); 11–46 min from decision to apply is an
    91	  estimate (⚠️), measured first during rollout against a 30-minute target.
    92	- **Blockers to know:** a risky change already waiting on `main` blocks your fix for that stack until
    93	  it is approved or reverted; at night, process files (workflows, `CLAUDE.md`, catalogue) wait for the
    94	  L3 owner team, or the JIT fallback applies.
    95	- **Only if the PR path cannot be used** (GitHub Actions down, broken pipeline, an operation not in
    96	  IaC): end your AWS portal session and sign in fresh, then request a JIT grant in the incident
    97	  channel outside GitHub, with the exact commands. The on-call approver approves before the grant.
    98	  You get `InfraOperator-<service>` (1-hour role session; the real window can approach 2 h) and type
    99	  the commands yourself, in a terminal **without an agent**. Afterwards your commands are compared
   100	  with CloudTrail (by hand in phase 1, by a job from phase 2), and you open a PR that codifies the change.
   101	- **Layers:** [3](01-framework.md#layer-3--change-workflow-by-risk-level),
   102	  [7](01-framework.md#layer-7--observability-audit-incident-response-and-break-glass); diagram
   103	  [`03-incident-lane`](../diagrams/03-incident-lane.svg).
   104	
   105	## 5. Reading real customer data
   106	
   107	- **What you do:** end your AWS portal session and sign in fresh, then request it with one tenant,
   108	  purpose, store, time window and the agreement that covers it. You get a data-read role for 1 hour.
   109	  After reading one tenant's data, do not post to shared places without review.
   110	- **Approval:** an approver who is not you, plus the data owner. At night the on-call approver
   111	  approves alone, and the data owner reviews it the next working day.
   112	- **PHI (medical records):** you read it yourself, in a terminal **without an agent**; give the agent
   113	  only a redacted summary. A store that holds PHI counts as PHI unless the agent reads a view without
   114	  it. Partner-uploaded claim documents never go into an agent session raw: reproduce with synthetic
   115	  documents, or de-identify them first.
   116	- **Non-prod** should hold no real data; a store not yet scanned follows this section's rule.
   117	- **Layer:** [6](01-framework.md#layer-6--data-protection-and-prompt-injection-defence).
   118	
   119	## 6. Adding a plugin or MCP server
   120	
   121	- **What you do:** open a request with what the tool reads, where it sends data and which write
   122	  tools it needs. A catalogue entry is added by a PR with a review record (examples
   123	  [`reviews/`](../examples/claude/marketplace/reviews/)).
   124	- **Approval:** the L3 owner team (the catalogue is an L3 path).
   125	- **Time:** decided within 5 working days (S6).
   126	- **Not allowed:** installing a plugin or MCP server outside the catalogue, or sideloading one with
   127	  command-line flags.
   128	- **Layer:** [4](01-framework.md#layer-4--supply-chain-for-mcp-servers-and-plugins).
   129	
   130	## 7. When you are the on-call approver
   131	
   132	- You are on a named 24/7 schedule: a primary and a backup. The primary approves; the backup steps in
