1	=== docs/adr/0001-prod-changes-only-through-ci.md
2	     1	# ADR-0001: Every production change goes through a reviewed PR applied by CI
3	     2	
4	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
5	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
6	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (Options §9, "A + D2'")
7	     6	- **Scope:** all writes to production AWS, GCP, k0s and Firebase; incidents included (k0s and Firebase
8	     7	  have no risk stop and no break-glass yet, G1, G2; human GCP access is open, G3)
9	     8	
10	     9	## 1. Context
11	    10	
12	    11	Engineering wants Claude Code to talk to AWS directly; Compliance wants no production change without
13	    12	a named human who reviewed and approved it. "Most engineers' profiles can reach production" (brief), and deploys from laptops are assumed
14	    13	(GĐ-10, unconfirmed), so an agent on that laptop can deploy too. Incidents are where the pressure to bypass
15	    14	review is highest.
16	    15	
17	    16	## 2. Options considered
18	    17	
19	    18	| Option | Pros | Cons |
20	    19	|---|---|---|
21	    20	| A. PR → approval → CI deploy for everything ("IaC first") | One path, approval before apply, evidence by construction | Slower incidents (est. 11–46 min ⚠️ vs 2–20 min, Options §6) |
22	    21	| B. SSM Automation runbooks with an approval step | Approval inside AWS | Not verified that it meets the approval rule (G6); only for operations someone scripted. Kept on the roadmap, verified in phase 2 (OD4) |
23	    22	| C. JIT direct access for the engineer + agent | Fastest | Approves access, not the change; agent holds prod write |
24	    23	| D. Hosted agent with its own identity | Clean separation | New platform; does not remove the need for approval |
25	    24	
26	    25	## 3. Decision
27	    26	
28	    27	"A + D2'": option A is the default path for every production change, incidents included. A narrow JIT
29	    28	fallback exists only when the PR path cannot be used during an incident (ADR-0005). The owner accepts
30	    29	that this fallback meets the approval rule only partly (Options §9 Q2). Incident target: ≤ 30 min from
31	    30	decision to apply.
32	    31	
33	    32	## 4. Consequences
34	    33	
35	    34	- **Positive:** the PR, its approvals, the run log and CloudTrail form one evidence chain keyed by
36	    35	  commit SHA. Agent-written and human-written changes pass the same checks (S10).
37	    36	- **Negative / trade-offs:** slower incident fixes; operations that are not in IaC must first be
38	    37	  written as code or a runbook. Two write paths remain (PR and JIT), while the framing asked for one.
39	    38	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the fallback stays narrow only if most incidents are expressible in
40	    39	  IaC (unknown, Options §8). Metrics: JIT grants per month, share of incidents needing non-IaC
41	    40	  operations; above about 25 % (⚠️ starting threshold), make the PR lane faster or add a runbook, never widen JIT.
42	    41	- **Example:** Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m. The responder's agent proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s in
43	    42	  `serverless.yml`; the PR is labelled `incident`; the on-call approver reviews and approves; CI
44	    43	  packages, previews prod and deploys with the OIDC role. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6).
45	    44	- **Next steps:** measure the incident PR lane on one service first (phase 1).
46	    45	
47	    46	## 5. References
48	    47	
49	    48	- Framework §1 and layer 3; `work/03-options.md` §1, §6, §9.
50	    49	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0003, ADR-0005.
51	=== docs/adr/0002-no-standing-prod-write-read-only-agent-identity.md
52	     1	# ADR-0002: Nobody holds standing prod write; in prod, the engineer's (and so the agent's) only standing role reads metadata
53	     2	
54	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
55	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
56	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (Options §9; D2)
57	     6	- **Scope:** AWS IAM Identity Center permission sets and SCPs on the prod OU; k0s, GCP and Firebase by the same principle
58	     7	
59	     8	## 1. Context
60	     9	
61	    10	On a laptop the agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and one portal session reaches every role
62	    11	assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate "agent"
63	    12	permission set therefore does not separate the agent from the engineer (⚠️ R2.9 #1). Whatever the
64	    13	engineer holds, the agent holds.
65	    14	
66	    15	## 2. Options considered
67	    16	
68	    17	| Option | Pros | Cons |
69	    18	|---|---|---|
70	    19	| A. Separate agent permission set, engineer keeps write | Looks like least privilege | Same SSO cache: the agent can still assume the write role |
71	    20	| B. No standing prod write for anyone; `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role | Agent cannot write prod with the engineer's identity | Engineers also lose direct writes and raw-log reads |
72	    21	| C. Separate OS user or container for agent sessions | Real separation of credentials | More setup; planned for phase 3 only |
73	    22	
74	    23	## 3. Decision
75	    24	
76	    25	Option B. Prod is written only by the CI pipeline role, or by an approved, time-boxed JIT grant
77	    26	(ADR-0005). The standing prod role is `ProdReadMetadata` [design name]: metrics, redacted log groups,
78	    27	configuration of services whose secrets are resolved at runtime; no data-plane reads of claim stores;
79	    28	1-hour role session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). From phase 2, SCPs on the prod OU deny data-plane reads and
80	    29	direct Lambda updates except for named roles (pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4, R4.6 #3). Option C follows in phase 3.
81	    30	
82	    31	## 4. Consequences
83	    32	
84	    33	- **Positive:** once standing write and broad read roles are removed (end of phase 1), an agent,
85	    34	  even a manipulated one, cannot write prod AWS or read AWS claim stores with the engineer's standing
86	    35	  identity (data-plane action list ⚠️ G13); k0s and GCP follow the same principle, mechanisms open
87	    36	  (G1, G3). In non-prod the agent keeps broad rights (`NonProdDeveloper`, ADR-0010 L1). Compliance gets least privilege enforced by IAM (S1).
88	    37	- **Negative / trade-offs:** during the transition, engineers lose raw logs and configuration of
89	    38	  services not yet redacted. Configuration values then come from the IaC code; raw logs need a
90	    39	  data-read grant in an incident. Process rules remain where
91	    40	  IAM cannot separate engineer and agent: no agent in the JIT terminal (D2).
92	    41	- **Risks & how we watch them:** SSO-token theft during a session could open later grants (⚠️);
93	    42	  mitigations [design] are a short portal session and a fresh sign-in before a grant. The data-plane action
94	    43	  list is incomplete (⚠️ G13). Identity Center assignment export is reviewed quarterly.
95	    44	- **Next steps:** phase 1 removes broad read roles only after the minimal real-data read flow works,
96	    45	  then removes standing prod write once its prerequisites are in place.
97	    46	
98	    47	## 5. References
99	    48	
100	    49	- Framework layer 1, layer 2 ("Trade-off on AWS credentials"), layer 8 rollout.
101	    50	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0005, ADR-0009.
102	=== docs/adr/0003-merge-to-main-is-the-approval-gate.md
103	     1	# ADR-0003: The merge to `main` is the approval gate: two people, code owners, on-call co-ownership
104	     2	
105	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
106	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
107	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-5, GĐ-8, GĐ-11; OD2, OD5, OD7, OD9, OD10, OD13)
108	     6	- **Scope:** GitHub monorepo rulesets, CODEOWNERS, `production` environment, on-call schedule
109	     7	
110	     8	## 1. Context
111	     9	
112	    10	Papaya is assumed to be on GitHub Team (GĐ-5), where environment required reviewers do not exist for
113	    11	private repositories (📖 R3.1.2), so the approval must happen before the deploy job. Incidents need an
114	    12	approver within 15 minutes, 24/7 (S7), and code-owner review requires an approval from an owner of the files (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7;
115	    13	per-file behaviour ⚠️).
116	    14	
117	    15	## 2. Options considered
118	    16	
119	    17	| Option | Pros | Cons |
120	    18	|---|---|---|
121	    19	| A. Upgrade to Enterprise for environment reviewers | Approval sits next to the deploy | Cost; not assumed (GĐ-5) |
122	    20	| B. Merge to `main` as the gate; `production` limited to `main` | Works on Team; the approver sees the code that will be applied | Nobody sees the prod diff before apply (partly handled by ADR-0004) |
123	    21	| C. More approvers for high-risk changes | More eyes | Slower; the owner wants two people per change |
124	    22	
125	    23	## 3. Decision
126	    24	
127	    25	Option B. Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
128	    26	approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
129	    27	push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5); branch up to date, since there is no merge queue
130	    28	(⚠️ R4.6 #1). `production` accepts only `main` (📖 R3.1.3).
131	    29	
132	    30	- **Merge = deploy approval** only if the reusable deploy workflow alone references `production`,
133	    31	  with no ref/SHA inputs, no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers, one
134	    32	  concurrency group per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4; ⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c).
135	    33	- **Two people per change:** one makes it, one approves it; the approver is always an engineer,
136	    34	  never an agent (OD2, OD5). L3 changes need one approver too, who must own the path.
137	    35	- **Incidents:** on-call engineers only approve; an incident responder writes the fix (OD7).
138	    36	- **Night coverage:** an on-call approver group co-owns every deployable path in CODEOWNERS; one
139	    37	  primary, one backup (OD9). It does not co-own process-defining paths (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS,
140	    38	  agent config, catalogue) or the SCP stack, which only the L3 owner team approves (OD13); IAM-only
141	    39	  stacks are deployable, so it co-owns them with the L3 owner team.
142	    40	- **Agent review:** an independent agent may post an automated review; it never counts as an
143	    41	  approval (GĐ-11).
144	    42	- **Cross-team PRs:** one approval is enough (OD10).
145	    43	
146	    44	## 4. Consequences
147	    45	
148	    46	- **Positive:** four-eyes enforced by GitHub, not by the agent; one rule for normal days and incidents.
149	    47	- **Negative / trade-offs:** GitHub accepts an approval from any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so the
150	    48	  on-call group can approve another domain's PR; domain review on normal days is a process rule.
151	    49	- **Risks & how we watch them:** admins can edit the gate, logged, not prevented (⚠️ R3.2.2, R3.6 #1;
152	    50	  logging 📖 R3.2.2); alerts on ruleset changes; monthly report of cross-domain approvals. An agent could approve through its engineer's login; no detection found (⚠️). The
153	    51	  required-check app's hosting, key and triggers are open (⚠️ G19).
154	    52	- **Next steps:** rulesets, CODEOWNERS and its validation check in phase 1; the required-check app
155	    53	  before any agent workflow may open PRs; L3 owner team composition open (G17).
156	    54	
157	    55	## 5. References
158	    56	
159	    57	- Framework layer 3 ("Gate = merge to `main`", "Who approves at night"), layer 7 (audit alerts).
160	    58	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0004.
161	=== docs/adr/0004-risk-stop-on-risky-prod-diffs.md
162	     1	# ADR-0004: Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until a stack owner approves the prod preview
163	     2	
164	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
165	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
166	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (OD8, OD11, OD13)
167	     6	- **Scope:** deploy workflows for Pulumi and Serverless stacks; k0s and Firebase not covered yet
168	     7	
169	     8	## 1. Context
170	     9	
171	    10	With the gate at merge time (ADR-0003), the approver reviews the code change, not the prod diff. A
172	    11	PR may not preview prod, because that would run PR code with state-write and secret access
173	    12	(📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). So a stateful delete or an IAM change can reach prod without anyone
174	    13	seeing its real effect. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files such as
175	    14	`serverless.yml`, not in separate L3 paths (assumed ⚠️; we have no access to the repo).
176	    15	
177	    16	## 2. Options considered
178	    17	
179	    18	| Option | Pros | Cons |
180	    19	|---|---|---|
181	    20	| A. Accept the gap | No extra step | Destructive diffs applied unseen |
182	    21	| B. Risk stop, approved by the L3 owner team | Specialist review | Often a third person; L3 team must be on call 24/7 |
183	    22	| C. Risk stop, approved by an owner of the stack | Stays at two people; works at night | Less specialist review; compensated by automated checks |
184	    23	
185	    24	## 3. Decision
186	    25	
187	    26	Option C [design]. The deploy job on `main` previews prod. On stateful replace/delete, an IAM
188	    27	change, a network or security-group change, or (from phase 2) an advisory policy finding, it stops
189	    28	and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a PR (the workflow does not, as "Allow GitHub Actions to create and
190	    29	approve pull requests" stays off, 📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3) adding
191	    30	`deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` with the SHA and preview hash (owned by the stack's owners and the
192	    31	on-call group, OD8, OD9); the first approver approves it
193	    32	(OD13). If that approver is unavailable, another stack owner approves; this makes three people and
194	    33	is recorded as a deviation (OD11). After the merge the workflow previews again on the new HEAD and
195	    34	continues only if the hash matches. Serverless uses `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI because
196	    35	differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2). A `mandatory` Pulumi policy violation always
197	    36	blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2; policy packs from phase 2).
198	    37	
199	    38	## 4. Consequences
200	    39	
201	    40	- **Positive:** the person who approves now sees the prod diff for the changes that can do lasting
202	    41	  damage. Still two people in the normal case.
203	    42	- **Negative / trade-offs:** while a stack is stopped, later deploys to it stop too (the hash
204	    43	  differs), including an incident fix, until the approval lands or the change is reverted. One more review round when the stop fires.
205	    44	- **Risks & how we watch them:** preview output may not be stable enough to hash (⚠️ Options §8); if
206	    45	  not, compare a structured summary. Until phase 2, the risk stop is the only compensation for OD8;
207	    46	  Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and policy packs follow. k0s and Firebase have no
208	    47	  preview step in this design (⚠️ G1, G2).
209	    48	- **Next steps:** risk stop in the deploy job in phase 1.
210	    49	
211	    50	## 5. References
212	    51	
213	    52	- Framework layer 3 ("Risk stop"), layer 5 (required checks); `work/03-options.md` §1.
214	    53	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0003.
215	=== docs/adr/0005-break-glass-is-time-limited-jit.md
216	     1	# ADR-0005: Break-glass is a time-limited, approved JIT grant, for incidents only
217	     2	
218	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
219	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
220	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-8; Options §9 Q2; D2; OD7, OD13)
221	     6	- **Scope:** AWS production accounts through IAM Identity Center; k0s and Firebase not covered (G1, G2)
222	     7	
223	     8	## 1. Context
224	     9	
225	    10	Some incidents cannot use the PR path: GitHub or Actions is down, the pipeline is broken, or the
226	    11	operation is not in IaC and has no runbook. Without a defined fallback, people keep standing access
227	    12	"just in case", which ADR-0002 removes.
228	    13	
229	    14	## 2. Options considered
230	    15	
231	    16	| Option | Pros | Cons |
232	    17	|---|---|---|
233	    18	| A. No fallback | Single path | Outage of GitHub blocks every fix; pressure to keep standing access |
234	    19	| B. Standing break-glass account, used first and approved later | Always available | Standing prod write; unapproved use, rejected by the owner (GĐ-8, Options §0.4) |
235	    20	| C. Approved JIT grant, 1-hour role session, command list, reconciled after | Approval before use; time-boxed; traceable | Approves a command list, not an applied change (partial) |
236	    21	
237	    22	## 3. Decision
238	    23	
239	    24	Option C [design], used only during an incident when the PR path cannot be used.
240	    25	
241	    26	- **Request:** command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub.
242	    27	- **Approval:** the on-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant; the on-call approver counts as
243	    28	  owner of the service (OD13).
244	    29	- **Grant:** `InfraOperator-<service>` [design name], assigned via `CreateAccountAssignment` and removed
245	    30	  via `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2); role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4).
246	    31	- **Execution:** the incident responder types the commands in a terminal without an agent (D2, OD7).
247	    32	- **Example request** (illustrative command ⚠️): "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage.
248	    33	  Run `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
249	    34	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
250	    35	- **After:** CloudTrail writes in the window are compared with the list; a codify PR follows by a
251	    36	  fixed deadline; drift detection runs until it merges.
252	    37	
253	    38	## 4. Consequences
254	    39	
255	    40	- **Positive:** no standing prod write even for emergencies; every use has an approval, a window and
256	    41	  a reconciliation.
257	    42	- **Negative / trade-offs:** meets the approval rule only partly (owner accepted). "No agent in the
258	    43	  JIT terminal" is a process rule: the grant is reachable from the same laptop.
259	    44	- **Risks & how we watch them:** deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions, so a grant
260	    45	  can run up to about 2 h (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which keeps
261	    46	  the user blocked ≥ 12 h (📖 R2.4.4); no night-time path to apply it is designed yet (⚠️ G20).
262	    47	  Metrics: JIT used where a PR was possible, writes outside the list, late codify PRs (review at 1).
263	    48	- **Next steps:** minimal JIT with per-grant CloudTrail comparison and a manual drift check of the
264	    49	  touched stacks in phase 1 (a temporary deviation from D2); revocation SCP and
265	    50	  automated reconciliation in phase 2.
266	    51	
267	    52	## 5. References
268	    53	
269	    54	- Framework layer 7 ("Break-glass = JIT fallback"); `work/03-options.md` §4b, §9.
270	    55	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0002.
271	=== docs/adr/0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md
272	     1	# ADR-0006: MCP servers and plugins are allowed only from a reviewed, pinned catalogue
273	     2	
274	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
275	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
276	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (framework approval 2026-11-09; rollout priority framing Q8)
277	     6	- **Scope:** Claude Code on all engineer laptops and in CI; Papaya's internal plugin marketplace
278	     7	
279	     8	## 1. Context
280	     9	
281	    10	Local MCP servers, plugins and hooks run with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5); remote MCP
282	    11	servers receive tokens and data. Papaya runs an internal plugin marketplace (brief, Appendix A), and
283	    12	engineers install MCP servers without review (brief); use of Linear and Slack through MCP is assumed
284	    13	(⚠️ G9). An unreviewed server or a plugin update can read the repo, the SSO cache or claim
285	    14	data and send it out.
286	    15	
287	    16	## 2. Options considered
288	    17	
289	    18	| Option | Pros | Cons |
290	    19	|---|---|---|
291	    20	| A. Free choice, guidance only | No friction | No inventory; any server can exfiltrate |
292	    21	| B. Denylist known-bad servers | Low friction | Misses new and changed servers |
293	    22	| C. Allowlist (catalogue) enforced by managed settings | Inventory and supplier records; blocks unknown servers | Up to 5 working days' wait for a new tool (S6) |
294	    23	
295	    24	## 3. Decision
296	    25	
297	    26	Option C. The catalogue is a file in git, changed by PR under the L3 owner team.
298	    27	
299	    28	- **Plugins:** only Papaya's marketplace via managed `strictKnownMarketplaces`, plus
300	    29	  `blockedMarketplaces` (📖 R1.4.2); sources pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only);
301	    30	  `disableSideloadFlags` (📖 R1.4.2); version floor covering the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
302	    31	- **MCP:** `allowedMcpServers` with `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4); match by
303	    32	  `serverUrl` or `serverCommand` (exact argv), never `serverName`, which "is not a security control"
304	    33	  (📖 R1.3.3); `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7).
305	    34	- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher, local or remote, what it reads and where it sends data,
306	    35	  supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status, no token passthrough (📖 R6.4.2), pinned version.
307	    36	  Example entry: `serverCommand` = `["npx", "<package>@<exact-version>"]` [design; placeholder].
308	    37	- **CI:** server-managed settings do not reach a CI job (📖 R1.7.10); CI uses a managed-settings
309	    38	  file on the runner and a fixed MCP set, because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
310	    39	  (📖 R1.3.5).
311	    40	
312	    41	## 4. Consequences
313	    42	
314	    43	- **Positive:** Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier records (P4c); unknown servers are
315	    44	  refused before they load.
316	    45	- **Negative / trade-offs:** waiting time for new tools; review effort for 1–2 DevSecOps people.
317	    46	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the enforced copy lives in server-managed settings, edited in the
318	    47	  admin console by Owners, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports and diffs it with git monthly until
319	    48	  G18 is solved (ADR-0007). `disableSideloadFlags` does not cover `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add`
320	    49	  (📖 R1.4.2), so the MCP allowlist must be locked. No per-group targeting in server-managed settings
321	    50	  (📖 R1.1.6). Tool description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️). Without MDM, laptops can
322	    51	  bypass server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11). Evidence: OTel `plugin_installed` /
323	    52	  `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6).
324	    53	- **Next steps:** catalogue v1 in phase 1 (may slip to phase 2 only with owner agreement).
325	    54	
326	    55	## 5. References
327	    56	
328	    57	- Framework layer 4; layer 8 rollout.
329	    58	- Related: ADR-0007.
330	=== docs/adr/0007-agent-settings-are-hygiene-not-the-boundary.md
331	     1	# ADR-0007: Claude Code managed settings are hygiene, not the security boundary
332	     2	
333	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
334	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
335	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-6, Options §0.4; D1, D3; OD4, OD7b, OD12)
336	     6	- **Scope:** Claude Code on laptops (server-managed settings, Team plan) and in CI
337	     7	
338	     8	## 1. Context
339	     9	
340	    10	The brief names "permission prompts turned off" as a problem. It is tempting to make Claude Code
341	    11	settings the main control. But server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not a security
342	    12	boundary" (📖 R1.1.7), local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8), Bash rules are not a boundary
343	    13	(📖 R1.2.6), and on laptops without MDM another login or provider skips server-managed settings
344	    14	(📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11).
345	    15	
346	    16	## 2. Options considered
347	    17	
348	    18	| Option | Pros | Cons |
349	    19	|---|---|---|
350	    20	| 0. Today (brief): some engineers turn prompts off; no organization policy is described (P3c) | No friction | Prompts turned off unnoticed; no evidence |
351	    21	| A. Settings as the boundary (lock everything, block auto mode) | Simple story | Bypassable on laptops; high friction; people work around it |
352	    22	| B. Settings as hygiene; IAM and the CI gate as the boundary | Boundary holds even if settings are bypassed | Settings give weaker guarantees than they appear to |
353	    23	
354	    24	## 3. Decision
355	    25	
356	    26	Option B. The boundary is IAM (ADR-0002) and the merge gate (ADR-0003). Managed settings set safe,
357	    27	uniform defaults:
358	    28	
359	    29	- `permissions.defaultMode` = `"default"` (Manual), with a read-only allowlist that excludes `aws`, `pulumi`,
360	    30	  `serverless` (D1, OD7b; 📖 R6.9.3); auto mode stays available and is measured.
361	    31	- `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` (📖 R1.2.2); `requiredMinimumVersion` floor (📖 R1.1.13).
362	    32	- Sandbox with `~/.aws` hidden (📖 R1.6.3, R1.6.4) [design]; `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` in
363	    33	  `sandbox.excludedCommands` [design]; `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` kept `true` (OD12, 📖 R5.5.5b).
364	    34	- OTel exporter without prompt content (📖 R1.1.20, R5.5.4).
365	    35	
366	    36	Outside managed settings: the `--restricted` flag (📖 R6.9.1b) in CI, set in the workflow file under
367	    37	CODEOWNERS, and, as a process rule, in the incident-analysis session; a setting cannot force it
368	    38	(📖 R6.9.1) (D3).
369	    39	
370	    40	Phase 1 ships `defaultMode`, the allowlist, bypass removal, the catalogue keys, the version floor and
371	    41	OTel; the rest of the baseline follows in phase 2 (OD4).
372	    42	
373	    43	## 4. Consequences
374	    44	
375	    45	- **Positive:** a bypassed or misconfigured agent still cannot write prod or read AWS PHI
376	    46	  stores with the engineer's standing identity, once standing write is removed (PHI paths outside IAM
377	    47	  are process-only, ADR-0009). Compliance gets
378	    48	  one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices.
379	    49	- **Negative / trade-offs:** more prompts than auto mode; a prompt for every `aws` read. S5
380	    50	  ("nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed") is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
381	    51	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the auto-mode classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions
382	    52	  (📖 R6.3.5); fallback to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers it (D1). The live
383	    53	  settings are edited in the admin console, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports them monthly and
384	    54	  diffs them with git until a better method exists (G18).
385	    55	  Until phase 2 there is no sandbox: `~/.aws` is readable and the network open; in auto mode the
386	    56	  classifier is the only gate. `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` run outside the sandbox even later
387	    57	  (📖 R1.6.4; ⚠️ inference): repo code that the agent can edit (Pulumi programs, Serverless
388	    58	  plugins) then runs with network and `~/.aws`, and SSO-token theft remains possible; bounded by
389	    59	  ADR-0002. With OD12, Manual mode does not mean a prompt for every command (📖 R5.5.5b).
390	    60	- **Next steps:** phase-1 subset; planted-injection test in phase 3.
391	    61	
392	    62	## 5. References
393	    63	
394	    64	- Framework layer 2; layer 8 rollout; research 6.6 (D1–D3).
395	    65	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0006.
396	=== docs/adr/0008-oidc-no-long-lived-ci-keys.md
397	     1	# ADR-0008: CI uses OIDC; no long-lived CI keys, with one time-boxed exception
398	     2	
399	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
400	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
401	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (framing Q8; OD1, OD6; target S2)
402	     6	- **Scope:** GitHub Actions deploy workflows to AWS, GCP, k0s and Firebase
403	     7	
404	     8	## 1. Context
405	     9	
406	    10	CI becomes the only routine production writer (ADR-0001), so it is the main target. Repository
407	    11	secrets can be read by anyone with write access (📖 R3.5.3b), which, in the single monorepo, likely includes every engineer (⚠️ assumed) and their
408	    12	agent. A long-lived key there is standing prod write in disguise.
409	    13	
410	    14	## 2. Options considered
411	    15	
412	    16	| Option | Pros | Cons |
413	    17	|---|---|---|
414	    18	| A. Keep stored keys, rotate them | No migration | Standing prod write for all writers |
415	    19	| B. OIDC everywhere, no exception | S2 = 0 | k0s and Firebase may not support it yet (G1, G2) |
416	    20	| C. OIDC for AWS and GCP; a controlled exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials | Removes most keys now | One exception to manage |
417	    21	
418	    22	## 3. Decision
419	    23	
420	    24	Option C.
421	    25	
422	    26	- **AWS:** GitHub OIDC (📖 R3.4.1); the prod role trusts only the `production` environment of the
423	    27	  monorepo (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4), ideally narrowed by `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
424	    28	- **GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization (📖 R3.4.5b).
425	    29	- **k0s/Firebase exception** (OD1, OD6): CI deploy credentials only, until it is checked whether they
426	    30	  can use OIDC. Conditions [design]: a `production` environment secret, never a repository secret
427	    31	  (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3); GitHub-hosted runners, because on self-hosted runners environment secrets act
428	    32	  like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5); if k0s needs a self-hosted runner, it is dedicated to the
429	    33	  `production` deploy and the residual risk is recorded (⚠️ G15); a single source of truth; owner, expiry, rotation.
430	    34	- `GITHUB_TOKEN` default "restricted" (📖 R3.5.3); actions pinned by lockfile or full SHA (📖 R3.5.5).
431	    35	
432	    36	## 4. Consequences
433	    37	
434	    38	- **Positive:** no stored AWS or GCP keys to leak (S2); every deploy credential is tied to a reviewed
435	    39	  workflow on `main`.
436	    40	- **Negative / trade-offs:** one-time migration; slower action updates. The exception remains until
437	    41	  G1/G2 are solved.
438	    42	- **Risks & how we watch them:** admins can change or delete the environment, and a deleted
439	    43	  environment comes back without protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); alerts and a settings comparison cover it.
440	    44	  The GitHub Apps used for CI agents and the required check have their own keys (⚠️ G19).
441	    45	  Runtime credentials inside the cluster are out of the exception (OD6).
442	    46	- **Next steps:** OIDC and removal of stored keys in phase 1; k0s/Firebase credentials moved to
443	    47	  environment secrets before standing prod write is removed.
444	    48	
445	    49	## 5. References
446	    50	
447	    51	- Framework layer 1 ("CI → AWS", "CI → GCP"), layer 5 ("Credentials").
448	    52	- Related: ADR-0001.
449	=== docs/adr/0009-agent-stays-outside-phi.md
450	     1	# ADR-0009: The coding agent stays outside PHI; real-data reads are approved per tenant
451	     2	
452	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
453	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
454	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (research 1.9, 5.8 "not extended"; GĐ-9, GĐ-14)
455	     6	- **Scope:** coding-agent sessions on laptops and in CI; production stores of all insurer tenants
456	     7	
457	     8	## 1. Context
458	     9	
459	    10	Papaya holds medical records, national IDs and bank accounts for several insurer tenants in
460	    11	different countries. Claude Team is not shown as BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Partner-uploaded claim
461	    12	documents are both PHI and a prompt-injection vector (research 1.11.4 L6). Neither OWASP nor NIST
462	    13	knows a full prevention for prompt injection (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
463	    14	
464	    15	## 2. Options considered
465	    16	
466	    17	| Option | Pros | Cons |
467	    18	|---|---|---|
468	    19	| A. Agent reads prod data freely | Fastest debugging | PHI in transcripts; injection can exfiltrate; no BAA |
469	    20	| B. Agent never reads any customer data | Simplest rule | Blocks legitimate debugging of non-PHI data |
470	    21	| C. Agent outside PHI; other personal data case by case under an approved, per-tenant grant | Matches the owner's boundary; debugging still possible | Process controls on some paths |
471	    22	
472	    23	## 3. Decision
473	    24	
474	    25	Option C.
475	    26	
476	    27	- **PHI:** never in an agent session. A human reads in a terminal without an agent and gives the
477	    28	  agent a redacted summary. A store that holds PHI counts as PHI unless the agent reads a view without
478	    29	  it [design].
479	    30	- **Other personal data:** readable within an approved request naming one tenant, purpose, store,
480	    31	  window and agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9); approved by an approver ≠ requester and
481	    32	  co-approved by the tenant's data owner [design]; data-read role, 1 h [design]. The same request
482	    33	  applies when a human reads PHI. At night the
483	    34	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day [design].
484	    35	- **Partner documents:** reproduced with synthetic documents or de-identified first [design].
485	    36	- **Non-prod:** synthetic or masked only (GĐ-14); no prod copies (S11).
486	    37	
487	    38	This is a target, not a guarantee: "no agent in the PHI terminal" is a process rule [design] with
488	    39	the same weakness as D2, since the grant is reachable from the same laptop.
489	    40	
490	    41	## 4. Consequences
491	    42	
492	    43	- **Positive:** "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2); one record per
493	    44	  exception (S9). Assumes injection succeeds and limits what it can reach.
494	    45	- **Negative / trade-offs:** debugging with redacted or synthetic data; a request for each real read.
495	    46	- **Risks & how we watch them:** of the 17 paths to PHI (research 1.11.4), tickets, chat, pasted text,
496	    47	  admin pages, CI logs, prod AI traces and fixtures are covered by process only; k0s and GCP stores follow the same principle
497	    48	  with mechanisms still open (G1, G3). Per-tenant scoping through session tags (📖 R2.1.8) is
498	    49	  unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️). During a data-read window a stolen SSO
499	    50	  token could open the grant (⚠️, ADR-0007). Data-plane deny actions are incomplete (⚠️ G13). Planted-injection test in
500	    51	  phase 3.
501	    52	- **Next steps:** non-prod data scan and the minimal real-data read flow in phase 1; data-plane SCP in
502	    53	  phase 2.
503	    54	
504	    55	## 5. References
505	    56	
506	    57	- Framework layer 6; layer 1 (SCPs); research 1.9, 1.11.4, 5.8.
507	    58	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0006.
508	=== docs/adr/0010-risk-level-decides-who-approves.md
509	     1	# ADR-0010: Risk level decides who approves, not how many; non-prod needs no approval
510	     2	
511	     3	- **Status:** Accepted
512	     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
513	     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-14; OD2, OD3, OD8, OD9, OD13)
514	     6	- **Scope:** every change made by engineers and their agents, from non-prod to production
515	     7	
516	     8	## 1. Context
517	     9	
518	    10	Engineering says "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly" (brief); the need is speed. Compliance's
519	    11	sentence covers production writes only (framing §3.1). A single rule for all changes either slows non-prod for
520	    12	no gain or leaves high-risk prod changes with too light a review. The owner also wants every prod
521	    13	change to need two people, no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it (OD2).
522	    14	
523	    15	## 2. Options considered
524	    16	
525	    17	| Option | Pros | Cons |
526	    18	|---|---|---|
527	    19	| A. Same approval for everything | Simple | Non-prod loop slowed for no gain; high-risk changes get no extra scrutiny |
528	    20	| B. More approvers as risk grows (e.g. two for L3) | More eyes on dangerous changes | Breaks the two-person rule; slower incidents |
529	    21	| C. Risk level narrows who may approve, plus a risk stop; non-prod free | Fast where damage is small; specialist owners where it is large | One reviewer for high-risk changes can miss things |
530	    22	
531	    23	## 3. Decision
532	    24	
533	    25	Option C [design levels]:
534	    26	
535	    27	| Level | What | Approval |
536	    28	|---|---|---|
537	    29	| L0 | Reads: non-prod anything, prod metadata | none |
538	    30	| L1 | Changes in non-prod (synthetic or masked data only, GĐ-14) | none, author only |

142	   142	## Limits of the risk stop
143	   143	
144	   144	The risk stop answers one framework problem: on GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before
145	   145	apply (framework §1). It catches **risky prod diffs that nobody looked at**. It is not a boundary
146	   146	against **malicious or prompt-injected code that was approved**:
147	   147	
148	   148	- The stack's own code runs with the stack's prod deploy role: `npm` packages are installed before the
149	   149	  credentials, with install scripts off (OD22), but the Pulumi program runs during `preview` and
150	   150	  `up`, and Serverless plugins during `package`/`diff`/`deploy`. That code could call AWS
151	   151	  directly, or tamper with files the classifier reads, in the same job. The defence against it
152	   152	  is the PR review itself, and from phase 2 IAM Access Analyzer and policy packs (layer 5).
153	   153	- A stronger variant [design, not in the framework]: preview with a separate prod **preview**
154	   154	  role (read and state access, no write), run the classifier in its own job on a fresh
155	   155	  checkout without credentials, and assume the deploy role only in a later job after the stop.
156	   156	  It adds a role and a job split; it is an open question for the owner.
157	   157	- `pulumi up` previews again before applying. A change made outside the pipeline between the
158	   158	  two previews (JIT, drift) is not re-checked. `pulumi preview --save-plan` + `pulumi up --plan`
159	   159	  would bind the two, but update plans are experimental (📖 R4.1.3).
160	   160	- Concurrency: a running deploy is never cancelled, but GitHub cancels a run that is still
161	   161	  pending when a newer one arrives for the same group (📖 GitHub docs source,
162	   162	  `data/reusables/actions/actions-group-concurrency.md`). Some merged commits therefore have no
163	   163	  deploy run of their own; the newer run deploys them too, and the change record must link both
164	   164	  commits to that run. `queue: max` would give every commit its own run, but the same page says
165	   165	  the order "is not guaranteed": an older commit could then deploy after a newer one and undo it
166	   166	  in prod. So the default is kept on purpose [design].
167	   167	- The type lists are examples. For types that are missing, the rule on property names
168	   168	  (`policy`, `role`, `securityGroup`, `vpcConfig`, `public`, `authorization`, `logging`, …;
169	   169	  a narrower set on creates) catches some changes, not all.
170	   170	- **Code in the deploy job can act as either deploy role of its environment.** `id-token: write`
171	   171	  is job-wide, so the Pulumi program, Serverless plugins and any allowlisted install script can
172	   172	  request the job's OIDC token (⚠️ from memory of GitHub's OIDC docs) and assume either role that
173	   173	  trusts that environment. Since OD22 (phase 1) that is a domain stack's bounded roles, never the
174	   174	  IAM stack's role (`production-iam`, E4), and no other install script runs
175	   175	  (`npm_config_ignore_scripts`). Still on the phase-2 roadmap with OD15: a separate preview role
176	   176	  and a build job without `id-token`.
177	   177	- **Open gap:** nothing proves that a deploy really stopped at `stopped_commit` with the
178	   178	  approved hash. An approval merged early (naming a commit whose deploy did not stop, with a
179	   179	  hash computed in advance, which needs knowledge of prod inputs) is accepted if a later change
180	   180	  **outside** the stack's directory, such as a shared library, produces exactly that diff. Changes
181	   181	  inside the stack's directory are rejected. Watching the whole repository instead would cancel
182	   182	  every approval at each unrelated merge in a monorepo. The fix is for the approval-gate app to
183	   183	  check, on the approval PR, that the stopped run's summary carries the same hash (G19) [design].
184	   184	  `test_known_gap_early_approval_and_change_outside_the_stack` documents the current behaviour.

## Findings from writing these files

Points the framework text does not yet say; carried into the framework in the final pass.
Owner decisions 2026-11-09 (framework OD14–OD18): findings 1, 3 and 4 accepted; the risk stop keeps
its current scope (OD15); the early-approval gap is an accepted limit for G19 to close (OD18).
Step 2: finding 16 accepted (OD19); the job-wide OIDC token limit goes to the phase-2 roadmap
with OD15 (OD20). After the independent review (2026-11-09), OD22 moves the per-environment roles
into phase 1.

1. **The risk-stop classifier must be an L3 path** [design]. The deploy runs it from the merged
   commit, so a PR that edits it together with an IAM change, approved by the domain team, could
   switch the stop off. `CODEOWNERS` adds `/tools/risk-stop/` to the L3 owner team. Needs owner
   confirmation: it extends the canonical L3 list of framework layer 5.
2. **An approval must be bound to git history, not only to a hash** [design]. Two review rounds
   found ways for one PR to carry its own risky change and approval, or for an approval to be
   reused. Rules now: read from git objects only; file named `<stopped_commit>.yaml`, never
   edited; stopped commit and approval commit both on `main`'s first-parent history, in that
   order; the approval commit touches only `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`; the stack's directory
   and the classifier unchanged since the stopped commit; at most 7 days old.
3. **Squash-only merges** [design]: `ruleset-main.json` allows only squash, so each PR is one
   commit on `main`. Cost: PR-internal history is not kept on `main`.
4. **Deploy only the tip of `main`** [design]: people with write access can re-run a workflow run
   for up to 30 days, with the same `GITHUB_SHA` (📖 GitHub docs source,
   `content/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs.md`, via review). An
   old deploy run re-run would roll prod back without any approval. `deploy-prod.yml` stops unless
   the run's commit is the current tip of `main`, read with `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/heads/main`
   (✅ branch-only form; `commits/main` could resolve to a tag named `main`). This is a new
   condition for framework layer 3's "merge approval = deploy approval" list.
5. **Classification beyond the framework's categories** [design]: the property-name rule, the
   audit/detection category and "an unknown operation stops" go beyond layer 3's list
   (stateful replace/delete, IAM, network, policy finding).
6. **The approval hash must cover changed values**, not only resource names, or an approval for
   one IAM policy would let a different change to the same policy through; and it must leave out
   values that change on every build, or an approval never matches. ⚠️ From memory, not checked:
   Serverless puts a timestamped path in the Lambda `Code.S3Key` and a code hash in
   `AWS::Lambda::Version` logical IDs; both are left out of the hash.
7. **Fail-safe CODEOWNERS default** [design]: without it, root `package.json`, a new stack or a new
   `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` folder would be unowned, and GitHub then accepts an approval from
   any writer (📖 about code owners).
8. **Same-repository reusable workflows can use `uses: $/.github/workflows/<file>`**, which GitHub
   now recommends: it resolves to the running commit, not to the runner's workspace (📖 GitHub docs
   source, `data/reusables/actions/reusable-workflow-calling-syntax.md`; flagged by zizmor's
   `self-repository` audit). `actionlint` 1.7.12 (✅ latest release on 2026-11-09, published
   2026-03-30) does not know the syntax; `validate.sh` ignores only that message.
9. **`runner.temp` is not available in job-level `env`** (✅ caught by `actionlint`); paths use
   `$RUNNER_TEMP` inside steps.

### Step 2 (identity and access)

10. **SCP "protect the org trail" is mostly redundant** for member accounts: they cannot delete
    an organization trail or turn its logging off anyway (📖 R2.6.2). E5 instead denies changes
    to any trail inside prod accounts. The framework's layer-1 bullet is reworded in the final pass.
11. **"Metadata" reads can leak configuration, data or secrets** (⚠️ response contents from
    memory of the API references): `lambda:ListFunctions` and `ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition` return
    environment variables and cannot be limited to one resource (✅ catalogue: not resource-scoped);
    `lambda:GetFunction` also returns a code download URL; `ecs:DescribeTasks` returns container
    environment overrides; `cloudformation:DescribeStacks` returns stack outputs (it could be scoped
    per stack); `cloudformation:DescribeStackEvents` returns `ResourceProperties`, "the properties
    used to create the resource" (📖 [StackEvent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/APIReference/API_StackEvent.html)),
    which for a function includes its environment variables (⚠️ inferred); `logs:DescribeQueries`
    returns other users' query strings. E6 leaves all of them out [design];
    `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` is granted per function instead.
12. **AWS's annotations are signals, not a classification of customer data**: `IsDataPlane` marks
    `cloudwatch:GetMetricData` too; `sqs:ListQueues` is not marked `IsList`; and many `IsList`
    actions return data or configuration (`s3:ListBucket` object keys, `ec2:Describe*` launch
    templates, `ssm:ListCommandInvocations` output; ✅ annotations in the catalogue, ⚠️ response
    contents from memory). The tests use an explicit allowlist for `Resource: "*"`. One entry has a
    condition: `states:ListExecutions` returns execution names, so names must not be built from
    claim data [design].
13. **Two prod deploy roles** (framework layer 1 already implies it): the SCP exempts the Pulumi
    role from the Lambda-update deny, but not the Serverless role, so `serverless deploy function`
    cannot change a function outside CloudFormation (drift). It does not stop malicious code in
    the job (Limits). `deploy-prod.yml` has one credentials step per tool, so an unset role
    variable fails instead of falling back to the other role.
14. **The claim-data deny assumes a naming convention** [design]: every legitimate reader must
    match `app-claims-*` or a `DataRead-*` permission set. Lambda execution roles behind SQS event
    sources, Step Functions execution roles and an AWS Backup role that reads the bucket would be
    denied otherwise (only service-linked roles are outside SCPs, 📖 R2.3.2). Phase-2 prerequisite:
    inventory the real callers of these actions (CloudTrail, IAM last-accessed data) and add them
    before the SCP is attached.
15. **The trail deny blocks every principal in prod accounts**, including deploy roles and
    `OrganizationAccountAccessRole`: a member-account trail can only be changed after a temporary
    change to the SCP (an L3 path), or an exempt audit role would have to be added [design].
16. **Exempt role names must be protected** (OD19): the exemptions are name patterns, so anyone in
    a prod account who could create or re-trust a role named `app-claims-*` or `cfn-deployment-*`
    would bypass both denies. E5 lets only `github-prod-deploy-pulumi` change those roles.
    - **Today that role deploys every Pulumi stack**, not only the IAM stack, and any job in the
      deploy workflow can obtain it (OD20). So "only the IAM stack" holds only after OD20 (since
      OD22: phase 1, E4, E4b) gives the
      IAM stack its own role and OIDC subject; until then the protection is "only an approved prod
      Pulumi deploy" (agent's reading of OD19, confirmed by the owner 2026-11-09).
    - **Residual risks:** a principal that may pass an `app-claims-*` role could create a new
      function with it (`lambda:CreateFunction` is not denied), and one that may pass
      `cfn-deployment-*` to CloudFormation could change any function through a template;
      `iam:PassRole` is left out on purpose because the Serverless role must pass
      `cfn-deployment-*`. An `InfraOperator-*` grant may change an `app-claims` function's code
      and so read claim data indirectly (accepted with break-glass, ADR-0005; JIT reconciliation
      in layer 7 is the control).
    - **Constraints and prerequisites (phase 2):** Serverless services cannot create their own
      `app-claims-*` execution roles (CloudFormation runs as `cfn-deployment-*`, not exempt); those
      roles live in the Pulumi IAM stack and are referenced by ARN. The protected roles must exist
      before the SCP is attached, and if `github-prod-deploy-pulumi`'s own trust breaks (e.g. the
      subject-format opt-in of E4), only an SCP change from the management account (an L3 path)
      can repair it.
17. **Gaps in the claim-data deny, under G13** (⚠️ not verified): S3 requests through access
    points may be authorised on the access-point ARN, not the bucket ARN; KMS `Decrypt` on the
    claim keys would be a second layer.
    The deny also covers `sqs:StartMessageMoveTask` (a write, ✅ catalogue), which could move claim
    messages to another queue; cost: a JIT grant cannot redrive a claims dead-letter queue.

### Step 3 (agent runtime, supply chain, policy pack)

18. **The settings schema on schemastore.org is community-maintained and lags behind**: it accepts
    unknown keys and lacks `allowedProviders` and `managedSourcesBehavior` (✅ checked). The tests
    therefore check keys by path and require a documentation source for every key it lacks.
19. **The phase-1 allowlist gives no protection for `~/.aws`, and a "read-only" wildcard rule
    can write files** (review step 3): Claude Code runs a built-in set of read-only commands
    (`cat`, `grep`, `head`, read-only `git` …) without a prompt in every mode, and the set is not
    configurable (📖 [permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md#read-only-commands)).
    Leaving `cat` out of the allowlist protected nothing. Worse, `Bash(git log *)`, `Bash(git show *)`
    and `Bash(git diff *)` also match `--output=<path>`, which writes chosen content to any path
    (✅ git 2.34.1; the docs use `git log --output=<file>` as an example match). The allowlist is now
    two exact repo scripts, and those run whatever `package.json` says [limit]. Owner decision OD21
    adds two keys to phase 1: a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule, which also applies to recognized
    `cat`/`head`/`tail` (📖 permissions), and `autoMode.classifyAllShell` (📖, ≥ 2.1.193), so the two
    allow rules do not skip the auto-mode classifier. Left open until the phase-2 sandbox: a command
    that reads files without naming them (`grep -r` from `~`) or a script that opens `~/.aws` itself
    is not covered by a deny rule (📖 permissions). Not chosen: `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`
    (📖, ≥ 2.1.257), which would also block every read outside the repository.
20. **Credential paths beyond the HIPAA template** [design]: `~/.aws` as a whole (the SSO token
    cache opens every role of the engineer, layer 2), `~/.kube`, `~/.pulumi`, `~/.config/gcloud`,
    the Firebase CLI token, `~/.docker/config.json`. `~/.config/gh` must be hidden from the sandbox
    too, not only from Claude's Read tool: sandboxed commands run without a prompt (OD12) and
    `api.github.com` is allowed, so a readable token lets the agent approve PRs as the engineer (OD5).
    This closes only the sandboxed route: an excluded CLI (`pulumi`, `serverless`) runs repository
    code outside the sandbox with full access (finding 22), so hiding credentials from the sandbox
    is hygiene, not a boundary (ADR-0007).
21. **TypeScript 7 is not yet supported by `@pulumi/pulumi`** (✅ npm peer-dependency error:
    `typescript >= 3.8.3 < 7`); the pack pins TypeScript 6.0.3.
22. **`sandbox.excludedCommands` entries match like `Bash(...)` rules** (📖
    [sandboxing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md#run-commands-outside-the-sandbox-with-excludedcommands)):
    `aws` alone matches only `aws` with no arguments, so the first draft kept every `aws` call in the
    sandbox, where it fails (no `~/.aws`, no AWS endpoints). Entries are now `aws *`, `pulumi *`,
    `serverless *`. The docs also answer the framework's ⚠️ on matching: every command in the call
    must match; a call with `cd`, a redirect, `$(...)` or a subshell stays sandboxed; the match is on
    the text, so `/usr/local/bin/aws`, a script that calls `aws`, and `npx serverless` do not match.
    Excluded commands go through the permission flow: they prompt in Manual mode, but in auto mode
    the classifier decides (📖 sandboxing), so phase 2 also lists them as `ask` rules, which prompt
    in every mode (📖 auto-mode-config). The prompt shows the command (`pulumi preview`), not the
    repository code it runs, which a sandboxed command may have changed without a prompt.
23. **A mandatory Pulumi policy is only advisory while a value is unknown** (✅ `@pulumi/policy`
    1.21.0 `server.js` catches `UnknownValueError` and reports `advisory`). A PR-time or prod
    preview of a policy built from a resource of the same update passes; the stop comes during the
    update. Access Analyzer is the preview-time check (layer 5).
24. **The first policy pack missed the usual ways to grant admin** (review step 3): user and
    group policies, `AdministratorAccess` attached by ARN, `Role.managedPolicyArns`, and wildcards
    such as `iam:Pass*`. All are now covered and tested. Round 2: IAM also accepts `?`, so `s3:?*` and
    `*?` are full wildcards (📖 IAM Action element); covered too. Round 3: a wildcard in the service
    prefix (`*:*`, `s?:Get*`) is refused as a full wildcard (⚠️ whether IAM accepts it is unverified).
25. **The template's auto-mode `"$defaults"` pins keep the built-in rules in place** (📖
    auto-mode-config: a list without `"$defaults"` replaces the built-in rules; entries from managed
    settings cannot be removed). The first phase-2 draft dropped them, which would let a developer's
    own `hard_deny: []` discard the built-in data-exfiltration rule. Restored and tested. They are not
    a policy boundary: a developer's own `autoMode.allow` or `environment` entries still widen what the
    classifier approves ("the combination is additive, not a hard policy boundary", same page), and
    `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` does not cover `autoMode` [limit]. For prod CLIs the boundary is
    the managed `ask` rules plus layers 1 and 3.

1	# Reusable production deploy (framework layer 3 "Merge approval = deploy approval", layer 5).
     2	# The ONLY workflow that references the `production` environment. Called by deploy-on-main.yml.
     3	#
     4	# Conditions this file must keep (checked by examples/tests/test_workflow_policy.py):
     5	# - no ref/SHA input: it deploys the commit that was merged (github.sha of the push to main);
     6	# - one concurrency group per stack without cancel-in-progress, so a running deploy is never
     7	#   cancelled (Pulumi guide: that can leave infrastructure half-applied). GitHub still cancels
     8	#   a run that is only *pending* when a newer one arrives, so not every merged commit gets its
     9	#   own deploy run; the newer run deploys both commits;
    10	# - OIDC only (id-token: write); no AWS keys; every action pinned to a full commit SHA;
    11	# - it deploys only the current tip of main: re-running an old run (allowed for writers for 30
    12	#   days, same GITHUB_SHA) would otherwise roll prod back without any approval;
    13	# - prod preview -> risk stop -> apply; the risk stop step cannot be skipped or ignored.
    14	#   No --skip-preview/-f, --target/-t, --exclude, --replace, state, import, destroy.
    15	# - one GitHub environment per kind of stack (OD22): the IAM stack deploys from
    16	#   `production-iam`, every other stack from `production`. Each environment has its own OIDC
    17	#   subject, so its own deploy roles (examples/aws/): code running in a domain stack's job
    18	#   cannot obtain the IAM stack's role, the only role that may change SCP-exempt roles.
    19	# - no install scripts run (npm_config_ignore_scripts), except for the packages on the reviewed
    20	#   allowlist tools/ci/allowed-install-scripts.txt, an L3 path (OD22).
    21	#
    22	# Known limits (examples/README.md): the stack's own code (the Pulumi program, Serverless
    23	# plugins) runs with that stack's deploy role during preview and apply, so the risk stop
    24	# catches risky diffs nobody looked at, not malicious code that was approved; OD22 limits the
    25	# damage to what that stack's role may do. `pulumi up` previews again; a change made outside
    26	# the pipeline between the two previews is not re-checked.
    27	#
    28	# Variables of both environments (not secrets; same names, values per environment): AWS_REGION,
    29	# PROD_PULUMI_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, PROD_SERVERLESS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, PULUMI_BACKEND_URL,
    30	# PULUMI_CLI_VERSION, NODE_VERSION. The Serverless License Key is read from
    31	# SSM Parameter Store with the deploy role (sf >= 4.4.19, R4.4.8), so no CI secret holds it.
    32	name: deploy-prod
    33	
    34	on:
    35	  workflow_call:
    36	    inputs:
    37	      stack:
    38	        description: Stack name, e.g. claims-data. Also the deploy-approvals/<stack>/ directory.
    39	        type: string
    40	        required: true
    41	      tool:
    42	        description: "pulumi or serverless"
    43	        type: string
    44	        required: true
    45	      workdir:
    46	        description: Directory of the stack in the monorepo
    47	        type: string
    48	        required: true
    49	
    50	permissions: {}
    51	
    52	jobs:
    53	  deploy:
    54	    name: deploy ${{ inputs.stack }} to production
    55	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    56	    # OD22: only the IAM stack gets `production-iam` (and so the IAM deploy role). The mapping
    57	    # lives here, in an L3 path, not in a caller input. `inputs` is available in `environment`
    58	    # (✅ actionlint 1.7.12, which checks context availability, accepts it).
    59	    environment: ${{ inputs.stack == 'iam' && 'production-iam' || 'production' }}
    60	    permissions:
    61	      contents: read   # check out the merged commit
    62	      id-token: write  # OIDC to the prod deploy role; no stored AWS keys
    63	    concurrency:
    64	      group: deploy-prod-${{ inputs.stack }}
    65	      cancel-in-progress: false
    66	    env:
    67	      STACK: ${{ inputs.stack }}
    68	      TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
    69	      WORKDIR: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
    70	      # Every npm, npx and `pulumi install` in this job skips lifecycle scripts (R9.1.13: "npm
    71	      # does not run scripts specified in package.json files"; ⚠️ whether this covers every
    72	      # dependency's scripts is not stated, test on the runner).
    73	      npm_config_ignore_scripts: "true"
    74	    steps:
    75	      - name: Check out the merged commit, with history for the risk-stop approval checks
    76	        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
    77	        with:
    78	          persist-credentials: false
    79	          fetch-depth: 0
    80	
    81	      - name: Set up Node.js
    82	        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
    83	        with:
    84	          node-version: ${{ vars.NODE_VERSION }}
    85	
    86	      - name: Refuse to deploy anything but the current tip of main
    87	        env:
    88	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    89	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    90	        run: |
    91	          # git/ref/heads/main names the branch explicitly; a tag called `main` cannot match.
    92	          tip=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/git/ref/heads/main" --jq .object.sha)
    93	          if [ "$tip" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
    94	            echo "This run is for $GITHUB_SHA but main is at $tip (re-run, or a newer merge)."
    95	            echo "Nothing is deployed; the run for the newer commit deploys both."
    96	            echo "If no newer run exists (e.g. its message had [skip ci]), merge an empty change."
    97	            exit 1
    98	          fi
    99	
   100	      # Everything that downloads code is installed here, before the AWS credentials are in the
   101	      # job's environment, and with install scripts off (job env above). A script that does run
   102	      # (allowlist below) can still request the job's OIDC token, since id-token: write is
   103	      # job-wide, or leave a process behind (examples/README.md, "Limits").
   104	      - name: Install dependencies before any prod credential exists in the job
   105	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   106	        run: npm ci
   107	
   108	      # `npm rebuild <pkg>` runs the install scripts of the named packages only (R9.1.13).
   109	      # The list is reviewed by the L3 owner team (CODEOWNERS: /tools/ci/).
   110	      - name: Run install scripts of allowlisted packages only
   111	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   112	        run: |
   113	          mapfile -t allowed < <(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/tools/ci/allowed-install-scripts.txt")
   114	          if [ "${#allowed[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   115	            npm rebuild --ignore-scripts=false "${allowed[@]}"
   116	          fi
   117	
   118	      - name: Install the Pulumi CLI only
   119	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   120	        uses: pulumi/actions@8e5e406f4007fca908480587cb9893c07090f58d # v7.0.0
   121	        with:
   122	          pulumi-version: ${{ vars.PULUMI_CLI_VERSION }}
   123	
   124	      - name: Install Pulumi plugins and the policy pack before credentials
   125	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   126	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   127	        run: |
   128	          pulumi install
   129	          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/policy-packs/aws"
   130	          npm ci
   131	          pulumi install
   132	
   133	      # ⚠️ From memory, not verified: Serverless v4's npm package downloads the framework on
   134	      # first run. Running it once here keeps that download before the credentials. Whether
   135	      # `--version` works before authentication (R4.4.8) is also unverified.
   136	      - name: Install the Serverless Framework before credentials
   137	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   138	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   139	        run: npx serverless --version
   140	
   141	      # Two roles per environment (framework layer 1; SCP in examples/aws/scp-prod-ou.json): only
   142	      # the Pulumi role is exempt from the Lambda-update deny; the Serverless role only passes the
   143	      # CloudFormation deploymentRole. This stops drift from `serverless deploy function`. Code in
   144	      # this job can still request an OIDC token for either role of ITS environment, not for the
   145	      # other environment's roles (OD22; examples/README.md, "Limits"). One step per tool, so an
   146	      # unset variable fails the step instead of falling back to the other role.
   147	      - name: AWS credentials through GitHub OIDC (Pulumi deploy role)
   148	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   149	        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd # v6.3.0
   150	        with:
   151	          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.PROD_PULUMI_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
   152	          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
   153	          # The run ID in the session name links CloudTrail events to this run (layer 7 change record).
   154	          role-session-name: deploy-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
   155	
   156	      - name: AWS credentials through GitHub OIDC (Serverless deploy role)
   157	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   158	        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd # v6.3.0
   159	        with:
   160	          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.PROD_SERVERLESS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
   161	          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
   162	          role-session-name: deploy-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
   163	
   164	      - name: Preview prod (Pulumi)
   165	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   166	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   167	        env:
   168	          PULUMI_BACKEND_URL: ${{ vars.PULUMI_BACKEND_URL }}
   169	        run: pulumi preview --stack "$STACK" --json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"
   170	
   171	      # Serverless Framework v4 (sf-core >= 4.37.0 for `diff`)
   172	      - name: Package once and diff against prod (Serverless)
   173	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   174	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   175	        run: |
   176	          npx serverless package --stage prod --package "$RUNNER_TEMP/sls-package"
   177	          npx serverless diff --stage prod --package "$RUNNER_TEMP/sls-package" --json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"
   178	
   179	      # Risk stop (layer 3). Exit 0: no risky change, or a valid approval matches this preview.
   180	      # Exit 3: risky change without a valid approval. Exit 2: unreadable preview. Any non-zero
   181	      # exit fails the job here, before any Apply step. The summary goes to the job summary and
   182	      # lists resource type, name, operation and changed property names, never values.
   183	      - name: Risk stop
   184	        run: >-
   185	          python3 tools/risk-stop/classify.py
   186	          --tool "$TOOL" --preview "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"
   187	          --approvals "deploy-approvals/$STACK" --repo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --workdir "$WORKDIR"
   188	          --summary "$RUNNER_TEMP/risk-summary.md"

   190	      - name: Keep the filtered preview summary as evidence
   191	        if: always()
   192	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
   193	        with:
   194	          name: risk-summary-${{ inputs.stack }}
   195	          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/risk-summary.md
   196	          if-no-files-found: ignore
   197	
   198	      # --yes is needed in CI (no terminal). Pulumi previews again before applying; a mandatory
   199	      # policy violation stops the update (R4.2.2). This is the phase-2 shape: until the policy
   200	      # pack exists (phase 2, layer 5), drop --policy-pack here and its install step above.
   201	      - name: Apply (Pulumi)
   202	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   203	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   204	        env:
   205	          PULUMI_BACKEND_URL: ${{ vars.PULUMI_BACKEND_URL }}
   206	        run: pulumi up --stack "$STACK" --yes --policy-pack "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/policy-packs/aws"

   208	      - name: Apply (Serverless), deploying the package that was diffed
   209	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   210	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   211	        run: npx serverless deploy --stage prod --package "$RUNNER_TEMP/sls-package"
